reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of the highlights of the Bali trip !!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited one of the most picturesque spots in Bali—Kelingking Beach—on a rainy day. Unfortunately, due to the weather, we couldn’t hike down to the beach. However, the views from the cliff were still absolutely mesmerizing. The sight of the clean white sand, turquoise waters, and the dramatic coastline was truly something to admire. There is a short walk from the parking area to the viewpoint, which is easy and well worth it. Even without going down to the beach, this place is a must-visit for its breathtaking views.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Special beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Really beautiful beach, beautiful sea and very suggestive natural setting.I highly recommend arriving very early, especially in high season.You can get there without any problems, even if the roads are a bit rough. Taxis instead arrive quietly.Admission costs €4.Pay attention to the timetable: if you arrive late and want to go down to the sea, the access becomes a single line under the sun, not pleasant.Overall very positive experience, just organize well.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Challenging climb
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Overall 4/5Location 4/5Environment 4.5/5Cost performance 4/5Very bumpy road from pier to the location! Deducted marks on the overall experience. View is good, too crowded to climb up and down with the various touristssssss

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Epic Views, Endless Vibes 🌊✨
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Our guide mentioned this spot has over a million Instagram followers—and it’s easy to see why! Standing here, halfway across the world, with this jaw-dropping view in front of us felt surreal. It’s the kind of place that makes you stop, breathe, and just take it all in. 🌊✨We didn’t make it down to the beach because we were short on time and had to catch the ferry, but if you plan to go, get ready for a serious workout—the stairs are long and steep. The beach below is absolutely stunning, but swimming is not safe due to strong currents and past accidents. Safety first!Soak up the view, snap those epic shots, and let this moment live forever in your memories (and your feed 😉). This is one of those bucket-list places you’ll never forget.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach but also very hot at the same time, very recommend to go there with your family and gangs. A lot of stalls there, good food and scenery

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Stunning! Very difficult stairs to navigate down to the beach. It is extremely hot, so take a large water bottle! Wear good hiking shoes and take your time

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wow beautiful beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: What a beautiful experience, to be on that spot. But really busy, some do take tich what pictures seems like a photo session. also saw that they were busy, to make an elevator, eternal shame it gets even busier

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nusa penida island is the best
reviewsWithKeywords.text: very nice, the view is still very beautiful, the sand very nice I had many very beautiful experiences in Nusa Penida. Thank you

reviewsWithKeywords.title: an overrated turist attraction.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Yes the view is stunning, but it is so overcrowded and has just become an overrated turist attraction.Been there, done that and never coming back again.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The worst kind of development
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Just sad…. There appears to be a very beautiful beach down below but the view is completely marred by a huge half-finished staircase (which will supposedly eventually include an elevator) on the northern half of the beach.  Not to mention the journey to this viewpoint is ridiculously difficult.  The roads are like the surface of the moon, filled with potholes the size of craters.  We were stuffed into a small 20-year-old SUV (3rd row inaccessible without opening a door) with four other tourists.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Don't waste your time going to this place
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nothing but a photo stop as you cannot go down to the beach.The route to reach the beach involves going down many steep steps .... need time and effort.Most people didn't go down.Very poor infrastructure in terms of shade, restaurants or roads.I recommend you to skip this place until the infrastructure improves

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Just insane, don’t waste your time…
reviewsWithKeywords.text: So they are building a lift at great expense and STILL the roads, if you can call them that, are downright dangerous, sort that out first surely!!! So once you get there you can feel free to join the 2 hr cue to take the completely unsafe stairs to the beach or perhaps instead, settle for overpriced tat at one of the extensive tourist trap shops, then, once you are suitably roasted to death, why not pay for toilet visit where you can get the 1950’s Turkish prison experience in the toilet, urine everywhere,  no flush, no lock, plenty of mosquitos though, then, once you’ve finished not being able to see anything, you can go back again the same horrific way you came, on a plus note, the monkeys are cool….

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: You need to come early – it gets very crowded later in the day. Some parts of the trail are quite dangerous. We only went halfway down, and it wasn’t easy, especially where there are no more steps.They’re building an elevator, which might ruin the natural feel of the beach. For now, it’s very hard to access and really only for those who are well-prepared.The road to get here is rough and risky, so drive carefully. There’s an entrance fee, 0,30 eur for parking. Also, be careful with the monkeys – don’t provoke them, as they can get aggressive.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Overloaded with people! But how beautiful it is though
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Visit with friends early August.The place is small, which makes promiscuity with other visitors almost oppressive. Many, many people.But it's normal, the beach below and the view are splendid! You'll get a lot of it if you can make your way through people.We greatly appreciated the monkeys scavengers with the careless "coughing ticks". I think some of them will never see their phones again! So be careful if you're an instagram addict.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Too many people
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very pretty but too many people. The road to get there from the port takes an eternity with the car runs. On the spot we have to queue to take a picture. If you are limited in time this site in high season is to be avoided. And if you have ever been to Corfu this site recall Agios Georgios. Everything around the site is very dirty.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Not worth it anymore.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach and the cliff seen from above is actually very nice, but: There are really hundreds of tourists out there, mostly tour groups, who then queue up for their always exactly the same Instagram photo. If you want to go down to the beach, you have to allow about 30 min for the descent and 60 min for the ascent, because the path is also supposed to be quite dangerous and we had children of primary school age with us we saved that. Worst of all, instead of better pavement of the trail, an elevator is being built to open up the last spit of unspoilt nature in Bali for mass tourism. As soon as this thing is done, the hordes that are currently only roaming at the lookout point will also be on the beach, then you can finally remove Kelingking from your To Do list. Bali seems to be gearing its tourism concept to Asian tastes, ticking off as much as possible in a short time with as little effort as possible, a few selfies, off on the bus and on. Too bad because the island could be so much more beautiful if you didn't design everything for mass and commerce.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beach with dangerous currents and waves
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It is a place where you absolutely must NOT swim as there are strong and devious currents (which you do not realize) and dangerous waves.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: It's an incredible view, clean. It's an incredible adem. It's an incredible sound. It's like taking a holiday to this beach again.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A very remarkable experience, enjoying a wave-wrapping wave-wrapping that rests my heart, I recommend to everyone
PARADISE, you take plenty of eyes from start to finish, despite the world up take your sneakers and go down to be little on the beach before the elevator is totally built.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A very sad sight
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The view is beautiful but at what price.You also have to look behind the scenes.It is so sad that a panoramic point is exploited in this way.Hundreds of scooters and cars parked a few hundred meters upstream.  Warong, shops of all kinds along the way. Hundreds of tourists playing neck and neck to get the best selfie. Plastic waste everywhere. Monkeys in the middle of all this garbage. I saw a tourist laugh at the sight of a monkey finishing his ice cream jar.And a gigantic elevator project to give tourists access to the beach... a project that disfigures the cliff tens of meters high.In short we went there and spread out after 15 minutes. I preferred to observe the local life along the road between Kelingking and Toya Pakeh, much more authentic.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A magical place despite some downsides
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Kelingking Beach literally took our breath away. The panorama is amazingly beautiful: this cliff diving into a turquoise sea is simply unreal. We quickly understand why it became an icon of Nusa Penida.But let’s be honest: access is not easy. The roads are frankly bumpy and tiring, and once you arrive, you have to deal with the crowds – even early in the morning, there are already a lot of people.What spoiled the magic a bit was the crane planted in the middle of the site, building an elevator. We understand the idea of facilitating access, but it distorts the landscape a little.Nevertheless, we have absolutely no regrets about our visit. It is a place to see at least once in your life.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: You slip you die ! But amazing view
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Amazing view, too much instagram picture womens … we tried to go down but we gave up at the last 100 meters because that’s really dangerous ! At the beginning you have the big stairs and then they become small and small to have at the part no more stairs, only rocks, if you like via ferata you will enjoy 😅 but with no security, if you slip you can die ! Good luck 🤟

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Just Wow
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Kelingking Beach really lives up to the hype! It’s absolutely beautiful, with stunning views from the top and that iconic cliff shape that’s so famous. The scenery is breathtaking and totally worth the visit. Definitely one of the most memorable spots I’ve seen!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: best part of Nusa Penida Island
reviewsWithKeywords.text: best part of nusa penida island.  a dramatic cliff shaped like a T-Rex, secluded white sand beach, and one of the best hiking spots in Indonesia.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Experience holidays to kelking beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I've been here a few times and it is a very nice view , and at an affordable price ,  I had a solo trip here, and also a private trip with family.  The tip is very safe. I'm carrying my little son.  One of the best trips I've ever had, the ship's fleet is very good and the crew is very friendly, so making my holiday and family more enjoyable, thanks to el moana bali who has given me the best trip experience.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing view
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very difficult access, but worth the sight. We did not descend to the beach because of the access to be quite complicated and need plenty of time. Always full, but you can take good photos.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A paradise that is shamefully coming to an end
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited this amazing beach today. We arrived by scooter after about 50 minutes of winding narrow road and with many potholes. Parked the scooter (5,000 RP) we headed towards the view point which is definitely crowded but beautiful. We were prepared for the descent with hiking shoes and they are served. Guys it is a difficult and dangerous path, despite this we have seen people do it in slippers but with disproportionate difficulties. In some passages it is no longer even a trekking but a real climbing.  Once down the place is magical. A paradise that at the moment remains quite exclusive because 80% of tourists remain at the view point given the difficulties of the route and this is good to not see the beach invaded by “tourists” hunting for photos from social media. Unfortunately they are building a monstrous elevator to get everyone down and soon it will become a place annihilated by the masses. Embarrassing that the government allows these constructions with devastating environmental impact. On the other hand there is plastic and waste everywhere along the way. A people completely indifferent to the unprecedented ecological disaster of which they are the architects.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very dangerous and full of trash
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very Dangerous and full of trashThe place is perfectly one of the wonders of the world.However, the risk of accident or even death on both the cliff and the beach (currents) is too high. Authorities on this island seem to care nothing about the number of deaths that have already occurred in this spot. It is a bit wild jungle more this culture and way of living/thinking

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning view
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited this place in May. We couldn’t go down on the beach due to time constraints. Someone said it takes around 1 hr to go down. View was stunning from above. I did go down few steps. The past is really small and little dangerous. You need to wear proper shoes.They are building an elevator now to go down, construction is in progress.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A Breathtaking Experience
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Kelingking Beach is one of those places that actually lives up to the hype and then some. Seeing that iconic T-Rex-shaped cliff in person is surreal. I’d seen it in countless photos before coming, but nothing prepared me for how massive and majestic it feels when you're standing at the edge, looking down. The hike down is steep, dusty, and the path can be a bit sketchy in places. It’s part climb, part slide at times—but absolutely doable if you take your time and wear good shoes.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The scenery from the viewpoint was truly stunning
reviewsWithKeywords.text: At low tide, we were reluctant to go down to the beach with our little kids. It was too dangerous for them. However, we could see the mantas swimming in the water from above.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wish fulfilled
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Amazing place, beautiful views, could not go down to the beach, did not have enough time and access is very complicated to return from below.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must-see! 100% worth it ! Highly recommended
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A real highlight on Nusa Penida! The view from the viewpoint is spectacular – one of the most beautiful beaches we have ever seen.But beware: The descent is very steep, narrow and partly unsecured. Good condition, sturdy footwear and no fear of heights are definitely a must. The trail is strenuous and can be challenging in heat – take enough water with you!Down on the beach, there are cold drinks, but they are much more expensive than usual – yet a lifesaver after the descent. The water and the sandy beach below are just fantastic. Those who take the road will be rewarded with an unforgettable experience.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: congestion and vulnerability to accidents
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The view is very good. Unfortunately, access to the beach is very dangerous in addition to a very long trap, I've been in the car for almost two hours

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning, But Be Prepared For A Climb!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is absolutely stunning, but you'll need sturdy shoes for the climb down and back up again. The steps are plentiful, steep, and rickety, so you'll need to be confident and fit to take them on. The view from the top, however, is undoubtedly one of the most beautiful imaginable and well worth the visit just for that.Also, the trip to this beach is something of an experience in itself, and it's VERY touristy. The roads on Nusa Penida are possibly the worst I've ever seen, but it's a scenic drive to the beach. Head down to the perfect beach, and you'll find you're pretty much alone to enjoy a swim in the picture-perfect sea.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning, imposing and unmissable place.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: An unforgettable experience! I recommend it to everyone who really likes to contemplate the beauty of nature. It's awesome! Standing up there on that cliff and seeing such infinity in front of you with an impressive set of mountains and a lonely beach, blows your mind. The road to get from the center of Nusa Penida on your own is very long and otherwise complicated. Now, though, is what I recommend you do.Renting a motorbike (which by the way cost very cheap and are in very good condition) and embarking on a trip barely dawns until you reach Kelingking Beach. It'll take you about an hour. It is a winding, dirt road and in some steep sections, but going slowly and with caution, nothing bad will happen to you.I clarify all this, because the other option to go, is with a tour. And I don't recommend that at all. Since when you arrive at the place, you will find it exploited with people, and the experience I assure you will be totally different than the one I tell you.As for the beach, you can go down on foot, but I didn't get to it. I stayed halfway as a precaution, took some pictures from a closer point and returned upstairs again. You have to be very well physically to be able to reach the beach, if or if with closed shoes and cap. At first, the descent is by means of a staircase made with the same stone of the mountain and with protection on the sides, but as the meters pass, it becomes more and more rustic, until it reaches the point where it is almost a crossing to be able to continue descending. In this part there is no protection at the sides and they offer only a thick rope (many years old) to assist you, but I recommend you to be very sure of what you will do since then you have to think that the same path you must do but in climb.I would definitely come back a hundred times more. If you're in Nusa Penida, you really can't miss it.PD: This section applies to all trips you make in Indonesia and especially if you visit this area: Be very careful with monkeys!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: WOWW
reviewsWithKeywords.text:

We look forward to welcoming you back to this stunning destination in the future.

Kelingking Beach Nusa Penida

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous, not for snorkeling
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is gorgeous and if you’re in the area I highly recommend going at the start of the day because there are massive crowds otherwise. The trek down to the beach is for the brave and fit. Once you are past the trinket shops, there is no paved path. You literally hike down a very steep, narrow mountainside with poorly maintained handrails made of bamboo or trees. I also wouldn’t swim here and have no idea why any would recommend snorkeling. Maybe those who do went during a different time of year but be aware the surf and current is rough and not even the locals suggest swimming here. Absolutely stunning beach though please just be aware before you go.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best vacation
reviewsWithKeywords.text: My vacation to Bali and Nusa Penida was an unforgettable adventure. The natural beauty of Kelingking Beach and the surrounding areas left me in awe, and the sense of tranquility on the island was a welcome escape from the hustle and bustle of everyday life. While the island's infrastructure is still developing, its raw beauty and untouched landscapes make it a destination worth visiting.If you're planning a trip to Bali, I highly recommend adding Nusa Penida and Kelingking Beach to your itinerary. Just be prepared for a bit of adventure and a lot of walking - but trust me, it's all worth it!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It offers some of the most amazing views in Bali and is well worth the effort to get there. Whether you’re hiking down to the beach for some solitude or simply taking in the scenery from the viewpoint, the experience is unforgettable.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning rock formation
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The Kelingking beach is about an hour's drive from the harbor. The roads to the harbor are narrow and broken at places, as are most roads in Nusa Penida. From the car park, there is a short walk through some shops to reach the path that leads down to the Beach.The views from the top of the cliff are stunning, and you can clearly make out the T-Rex rock formation. It's worth taking a lot of pictures from here. Watch out for monkeys though! There's a steep path leading down to the Beach—try this out only if you are really adventurous!There are a few stores selling souvenirs, water/juice, snacks, etc. There's also a money exchange outlet giving decent exchange rates.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Visiting Kelingking Beach was an unforgettable experience. The breathtaking cliffside views, turquoise waters, and iconic T-Rex-shaped rock formation were absolutely stunning. The hike down was challenging but worth it for the pristine beach below. A true paradise!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Kelingking Beach: Unforgettable experience, gorgeous, stunning beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Stunning and gorgeous beach.  All beach lovers must visit this one. Breathtaking beauty. Amazing colours of the water ..shades of teal, blue, green. Yes difficult to climb down to and climb up back again. Make sure you have 3-4  hours for this beach so that you get to it and swim.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Chinese at work
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The place is beautiful, so many people and if you are not trained and have hiking shoes do not face the descent that lasts at least 40 minutes and double to climb up. The view from above is spectacular in any case. The Chinese have begun construction of a mega elevator that takes you directly to the beach: how to ruin a magical place...

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Short busy and mesmerising visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the most beautiful beaches Sight is breathtaking. Avoid busy hours as it is very crowded. Little difficult with kids around youNo sitting place

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Highest recommendations!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This was the most beautiful beach I've ever seen. Very clean, not very crowded, and now that the summer is very great, it's definitely worth to visit. Highly recommend.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: best beach ever in Bali.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: this is the best view ever. pristine beach. not so many people down there due to the effort to reach down the beach at the moment i went there. We needed to be on boat from Nusa dua where i stayed with some friends. nice for instagram pictures.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Visit to the islands
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It's a beautiful place! We used to go there with friends. Quite a lot of people, but it's still worth it! Made a lot of beautiful shots.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fantastic view but very touristy
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We were there with children. We did not dare to descend at 36 degrees but the view from above is sufficient. Fantastic! It is of course very touristy and the driveway crowded.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Worth it!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Wow! Some level of fitness required. The climb down and up is quite challenging but well worth it. Highly recommend doing this early morning and not in the afternoon as it gets very hot with minimal shade on the climb. Do not wear flip flops, we chose to climb bare foot making it much easier for foot placement and less slippery. Stay hydrated and enjoy!! 😁

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning Views and a Rewarding Hike – A Must-Visit at Kelingking Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Kelingking Beach is a true slice of paradise! The stunning cliffside view resembles a T-Rex, making it one of the most iconic spots in Bali. The turquoise water and pristine white sand are absolutely breathtaking. However, be prepared for a challenging hike down, as the path is steep and rocky. Once you reach the beach, you'll find it to be less crowded than other tourist spots, offering a peaceful retreat. The waves can be strong, so swimming is not always safe, but the scenery alone is worth the trip. Don’t forget to bring water and wear sturdy shoes!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunningly beautiful!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Kelingking Beach and its surrounding cliffs are no short of spectacular, especially in terms natural beauty and photo options. If you’re young and fit I’m sure you may enjoy the challenging trail/steps down to the sand. In our case we decided we will only enjoys the views from above, which were awesome enough. At Kelingking Beach we arrived at 4pm while it was still sunny and remained till after sunset. Our driver, Putra was very helpful and talented in his photography skills. We stayed three nights on the island which was perfect for us however I would recommend everyone to stay at least one night. The day trip tour from Bali is very rushed and safety is compromised.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Option for relaxation
reviewsWithKeywords.text: For a relaxing moment it is worth it, on sunny days the water looks amazing. Good beach option in Indonesia. Good choice.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Crazy!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of the best sites in the world
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Make this your first stop when visiting Nusa Penida, and try to arrive early in the day. This is one of the most stunning locations in the world and a must-see for anyone visiting Bali. Only attempt the climb down if you're prepared for the challenging hike back up, as the ascent is steep and requires moderate trekking. Beyond a certain point, the stairs turn into uneven stones, making the climb even more difficult.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Kelingking Beach - Thrilling Road  and stunning view
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The road to Kelingking Beach is notoriously difficult, especially for those not experienced with riding motorbikes. The winding, narrow paths, combined with poor road conditions, like potholes and sharp, unexpected turns, make it challenging to navigate. Many tourists rent motorbikes to get there, but the lack of experience with such tricky terrain can lead to accidents. It’s definitely important to be cautious and maybe even consider hiring a local driver if you’re not comfortable with those kinds of roads.After parking, paying the small fee, and you can leave your motorbike safely, you walk through the village to the iconic viewpoint. The climb down the hill to the beach starts there.There are monkeys along the village and view point. Monkeys are indeed quick and opportunistic! They might look harmless, but their behavior can change quickly when they sense food or anything resembling it. Keeping food securely packed and being mindful of your belongings is important, as they won’t hesitate to snatch anything they find interesting.The descent to Kelingking Beach is steep and physically demanding, so it’s important to be prepared. The climb down involves navigating rocky and narrow paths, and while going down may seem easier, the real challenge is the climb back up. It requires good physical fitness and stamina, especially under the heat. Bringing plenty of water is essential to stay hydrated, and having some prior physical training will definitely help with endurance.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Unbelievable Views at Kelingking Beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Kelingking Beach is nothing short of spectacular! The iconic T-Rex shaped cliff offers one of the most stunning views I’ve ever seen. The contrast between the turquoise waters, white sand, and lush greenery is simply breathtaking.Getting down to the beach is an adventure in itself—the hike is steep and challenging, but once you reach the bottom, it feels like you’ve discovered a hidden paradise. The beach is secluded, peaceful, and perfect for relaxing after the hike.Kelingking Beach is a must-see for anyone visiting Nusa Penida. The views alone are worth the trip, and the experience is one you’ll never forget. Highly recommended for anyone looking to experience the raw beauty of Bali!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This was truly an amazing experience! One of the most beautiful scenes we have seen in Bali! Gorgeous views and a stunning beach. There are lots of people, but the beach is huge so there’s plenty of room for pics alone. Just a PSA, the hike down is HARD!! Not sure if someone has mentioned this in reviews but we heavily underestimated how steep it is. Be prepared for a true climb during the last half to the beach. The way up is better but this really isn’t for kids or older adults. Get ready for a true workout! If you stay at the top, there are ample opportunities for photo ops but you can also go a little bit further down and take some good solo shots without all the crowd. I highly recommend this for anyone coming to Bali!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Incredibly dangerous!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Kelingking Beach offers beautiful views.But (!) it is overrun by many tourists and the path that leads down is insanely dangerous, steep and insufficiently secured. Unfortunately, a young man slipped before our eyes and fell straight into the depths. We're not sure he survived that deep fall. When you get to the bottom of the beach, the sun pops improbably hot. No wind blows through the bay. You should never cool down in the water, as the current can carry you away in a life-threatening way. Unfortunately, there is little warning about this. Great respect is required on the way back up. The path consists of stones and steep slopes and many of the visitors developed circulatory problems due to the steep climb and the sun. Please take good care when visiting this spot. We only recommend a view from above and definitely not walking down the path with children or just flip-flops.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Breathtaking
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Stunning.A beautiful landscape.I explain below why I only gave 4 stars.Most people stop at the top of the steps, which is a shame, after which I can understand because the descent and ascent are very sporty.It starts with steps then it becomes climbing, so for adventurers remember to take suitable shoes, no sandals or taps, and especially do not be dizzy, do not forget to brush yourself with sunscreen.We went down with a 12 year old and a 9 year old girl (real chimpanzees), they had a lot of fun but the return was a bit trying for the girl, nevertheless she did!Downstairs, a beautiful beach, white sand and turquoise water, small cave and coconut trees to shelter from the sun.Watch out for the waves, swimming is a bit dangerous, the waves carry you away and they are powerful, we witnessed live an accident where a young lady dislocated her shoulder, she was rescued by boat.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful but dangerous and strong waves!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is indeed one of the most beautiful beach with blue water and golden sand. But, please be very very careful. Firstly, the hike up and down is tricky and dangerous. But, the waves were so strong that we fell in the water but managed to come out of the water but with difficulty. I wouldn't have gone near the water if I'd known about the strong wave situation before going or if there were any warnings signs (or may be I missed seeing the warning signs).Word of caution - Don't go near the water, its dangerous! Happy Travelling,PG

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stay Quiet and let beauty do the talking here.

This distinctive cliff has made the beach a popular spot for photography.The hike down the steep and rocky cliff to reach the beach is challenging. reviewsWithKeywords.title: Important! Needs preparation, it's dangerous. Very beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The most importantA very tough descent to the beach, at first there are normal steps, then there are vertical sections where you move like a rock climber. It’s realistic to pass for average physical training, with certain conditions1. Visiting time. Don't go after 11. It's unbearably hot, the descent takes 40-60 minutes. Narrow paths, part of the time you just stand, as people walk in both directions all day.I don’t see any point in going after 16. You can’t really see the sunset from the beach, the view is better from above, and getting back up is in the dark. We arrived at 8 am and spent the whole day there until 4 pm, this was the best option.2. What to take for the descent.- Good shoes are a must, ideally sneakers or sneakers; sandals are very dangerous. Since I was unprepared, it turned out to be easier to go down barefoot at the end. If you twist your ankle there, it’s unclear how they’ll get you out of there.- water- if you still go after 16, then a headlamp. There isn’t much of an option to hold a flashlight in your hands3. Waves on the beach. Be very careful. We were told that on this side of the island there are very treacherous currents and waves, you definitely can’t swim, people are jumping in the waves near the shore, I think it’s ok. There are several articles about those killed by the waves on this beach.4. What to eat on the beachThis is a very beautiful place. There are very few people in the morning, then there are more, but it’s quite comfortable. There is one “mini market”, bananas for 120 rubles each and other small expensive delights. We agreed back so that the guy from this store would carry all our things and we climbed lightlyOverall the place is amazing. And the feeling that you have overcome this steep descent adds some kind of pleasure to being there. It’s good if you have time to be there, I wouldn’t just go down to take a photo.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Serious physical training required!!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: First, the pros - this is truly one of the most beautiful beaches in the whole world - white soft sand, turquoise warm ocean, all surrounded by high mountains and greenery! There are almost no people (few people dare to descend). You rarely see such beauty. But for everything beautiful in this world you have to pay - I’m talking about the way down to the beach and back up. When I decided to descend, I read on several resources that “average physical fitness is required.” This is exactly what I have. BUT I want to warn many - visiting this beach requires much higher than average physical fitness! Comfortable shoes, water (at least 1.5 liters), and a hat are also required! Also calculate the time - the descent will take about 40/50 minutes, and the ascent will take more than an hour. Sometimes you need to climb almost a sheer cliff. There are huge waves on the beach - you also need to be very careful, since of course there are no lifeguards on site.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful View ... but unpleasant getting there
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beware - As stunningly beautiful this view and beach is, you need to consider whether it's worth the travel to get that 'Instagram' photo.Firstly, it's hazardous to those who wish to walk down the steep steps to the beach. Secondly, you can not swim on this beach as the currents are too strong, all the time.The view from the top is magnificent, but it's not a quick 5-minute car ride. Depending on where you are coming from or leaving from the Island, it's a 30 min + ride on terribly windy and narrow roads. This wasn't pleasant at all, and despite I've never got motion sickness, I felt unwell after this day trip.Many day tours from Bali (Sanur) offer snorkelling at Manta Bay, Gamat Bay, Wall Bay combined with lunch and 3 other land locations, including Kelinging Beach. This is way too much travelling for a day trip, and we even missed 2 locations due to running out of time. We left our accommodation at 7.30am and did not return until 6.00pm, that's fine, but the majority of that time was in transit, boat and car. I think if you were staying overnight on Nusa Penida, then a visit to Kelingking Beach viewpoint would be fine, but not during a day tour from Bali mainland. Trust me.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The route to the destination is winding and steep the whole way, and it's not very wide. To navigate the course, Papasan automobiles must make turns. If you plan on going down, you should try to dress warmly and wear shoes and long trousers. The road features both stairs and sheer rocks at various points along its length. Take it slow and easy. Extremely difficult, but the exertion is worth it when you get to the beach at the bottom. Consider giving it a shot.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best Beach in Bali
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Outside of Bali, this is one of the most beautiful spots in the world. Every traveller ought to make a point of visiting Nusa Penida. Amazing locations on land and in the water to snorkel with manta rays and other marine life. The most enjoyable ones are Kelingking and Broken Beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best View of Bali
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Kelingking beach absolutely lived up to all of the hype that it received on Instagram; this beach is incredible. The views were like something out of a movie, both from the cliffs that looked out over the water and from the trail that led down to the beach. It can get fairly heated, so going early in the day is highly recommended if you want to avoid the crowds. The island of Nusa Penida is well worth the time and effort required to get there. If you want to get a better look at this T-rex, climb a little higher up on the hill. There are various photo shooting spots available for you to snap the greatest photos, but in order to access, you will need to purchase some refreshments or food first. Sadly, there is trash scattered throughout the bushes in every direction. We can only hope that those who go there and those who are responsible for running and maintaining those locations become more aware of it.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sporty only if you want to go down
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the most beautiful beaches in Indonesia, but it is earned with the sweat of your brow, not to mention your body. Good shoes and a bottle of water are essential. You are ready for an exceptional experience. Be careful of the current but swimming is essential to regain strength for the return. Don't embark on the adventure without good cardio but treat yourself to an unforgettable hike that will stand you out from the crowd. Beautiful solidarity of people taking the risk of adventure.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must-see tourist spot
reviewsWithKeywords.text: After paying just under 5k to park our scooter, we were given access to the viewpoint. You pass many shops and restaurants/warungs on the way up. Once at the top, the view is breathtaking. As breathtaking as the hordes of tourists who risk their lives for the perfect Instagram photo. Tip: Continue walking, past the descent and the viewing platform (each costing 5k) into the 'woods'. Walk as far as possible. After a 5-minute walk you are completely alone and you have a great view of one of the most famous spots in Bali. There is a lot of waste everywhere here. So do your part and just throw your waste in the bin.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach worth the climb, but be careful and don’t wear flip flops
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We (a group of 8 friends) took a ferry from Serangan pier - it took about 1.5 h to Nusa penida and about 50 mins back. Then we rented scooters nearby and had a really nice drive to Kelingking beach. It was a nice view from the top, but looking down some of friends scared and didn’t want to go down to the beach (as 90 % of people) and one was scared of heights. Me and two friends went down anyway. The path is very very steep which makes it especially hard to walk/climb downhill. You sometimes have to wait for people going up as there is enough space only for one person on the path. You get dirty, dusty and scared for your life. However, when you come down it is totally worth it! The beach is not crowded, there is some nice shadow, you can buy some drinks and refresh in the sea (even though the current is too strong for swimming). Path down took us about 40 mins, but we were up in 20 - it is much easier to go up. If you only have limited time (one day trip) know that with hiking to the beach you will probably only have enough time to see this one beach (we were driving to Crystal bay afterwards but we only stayed there a couple of minutes - the beach is not as beautiful as Kelingking). Also on the way back the roads were crazy busy with cars and it was hard to ride the scooters. We managed to find one empty road so we could safely return to the pier. It was a fun trip overall :) Ps. Don’t wear flip flops or sandals for hiking to the beach! You will have to walk barefoot sooner or later. Bring sneakers.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Breathtaking view!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great view! Get there early! From 8:30/9:00 a.m. onwards, lots of cars/scooters with tourists arrive! We didn't go down to the beach. The descent was very steep, some of the paths were unpaved. We saw manta rays from above! See picture 2.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Simply beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: During our visit to Nusa Penida we visited this beach. The landscape from the cliff is stunning... the rocks below seem to form a dolphin diving into a cobalt blue ocean. A perfect trip to this fabulous island...

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The pearl of Nusa Penida
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It truly is the pearl of Nusa Penida!Superb site, breathtaking view, a must.Going down the 150 meters is difficult and the climb back up even more, in some places it's climbing.To do early in the morning before the day tourists arrive or at the end of the afternoon when they are in the cars to reach their fast boat.Bring good shoes, forget the tones.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: top location
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the most beautiful places outside Bali. Only about 40 minutes boat ride from Sanur. Nusa Penida should be on every traveller's list. Amazing places to snorkel with Manta Rays and places to visit on land. Kelingking and Broken Beach are the best. Sexy Taxi Tours on Penida and Bob Marley is the best.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful, Breathtaking, Challenging!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach and the view is every bit beautiful as the pictures say. The way to get there is pretty challenging makes the beach the ultimate reward when you get there. Know your physical fitness, wear good shoes, climb slowly and carefully. take a liter of water in your backpack. The water was perfect, it was a little rough. Great photo opportunities. The hike down is 25 mins and the hike up is another 40 mins. The hike up is definitely really difficult and will test your physical fitness.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Quite unique as a place of great beauty, access down to the beach difficult to access, very steep descent and many people count 40 minutes for the descent but it is worth it

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Magnificent to see absolutely….
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It’s a must-see place to do when you go to Bali and more particularly to Nusa PENIDA. The place is exceptional. We made the descent and frankly it was worth it. It’s physical and at times dangerous for some people, but when you get to the bottom: WOW, it’s GREAT. Allow around 1h30 down and up with more or less traffic.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very beautiful beach, I didn't go down because I was very sporty. I went there in the morning with a guide (13€) to visit the surrounding area on a scooter. At the end of September and early in the morning there were not too many people.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful cliff and beach in Nusa Penida
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Superb beach in Nusa Penida! Lots of people, but worth it. The descent is a bit difficult, but the beach is magnificent. Parking costs 5000 rupees and there are food options on site. I insist on taking sports shoes to make it easier for you to get down and back up and not to hurt yourself 🫶🏼☀️

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Dangerous access to the beach.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: No beach is worth taking such risks.Access to the beach is very dangerous. No indications or access limitations.Especially not to do with young children or if you are not in very good physical condition.In short, don't go there.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely views
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A place worth seeing. Beautiful views. As the main attraction of Nusa Penida, it is visited by crowds of tourists every day. There are big traffic jams on the way there because the roads are in terrible condition and very narrow. Parking is cheap but often crowded. Going to the beach requires a lot of effort and is not easy. You can meet monkeys on the mountain.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A mandatory stop if u are in Nusa Penida
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We, a family with one 7 year kid spent not more than 40 mins here. The view of the beach is breathtaking. There was a small contention for the photo spots. After that, we took some photos. But, the spots have very weak fences. One has to be very mindful of the same.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Climbing down is a memorable experience!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A stunning beach and a memorable experience climbing down to it. Yes, it’s tough, wear trainers, don’t carry anything unless it’s on your back and bring water. Harder than I imagined and my legs ached for days, but what an achievement when you reach the bottom! The steps end about a third of the way down, then it’s just rock climbing , so if you find the steps tough then turn back!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Recommended to get up early 🤓
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We went today. At 8 in the morning we were there and there were almost no people, no lines or anything. The views from above are already worth it. It is spectacular! We have gone down, the descent is a bit peculiar since you cannot go super fast either with flip flops or barefoot. You have to go with sneakers and there is no problem, it is not as complicated as they say, you just have to go little by little and holding on to a railing. It is true that it is not suitable for 100% of the population and that is why I do not give it the highest score.I put on a tracksuit to go down because I knew it was going to get dirty and indeed the black hands on the reed railing and the railing need to be grabbed, otherwise it is impossible to go down or up. It took us about 25 minutes to go down. There are a lot of waves down there, you can't swim as such because it's quite dangerous but it's worth going down. Below you can buy pringles, coconuts, drinks...The climb is more tiring, you have to hold onto some ropes and the railings. It took us 25 minutes to go up, stopping occasionally because people were getting off but not many. When we went up it would have been 10 or something and there were already all the lines, a lot of people and a lot of people arriving. We stayed in Nusa Penida for 5 nights, although it is worth staying some day to be able to go early because it has nothing to do with it 😊

reviewsWithKeywords.title: L’Époustouflante is worth it!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A panorama, a beach, water, waves… breathtaking!!!This beach is by far the number 1 on the island.Unfortunately terribly busy which makes its access even more sporty (and long)From the top of the cliff the view of the beach is incredible! Harmony of color, perfection of nature.To reach 200 m further down you have to take a staircase, first concreted, then a steep and very narrow path which ends almost in climbing mode. With the flow, allow 30 minutes to go down and 20 to go up. It’s quite physical because it’s very steep, all in the Indonesian heat!Bring water and a pair of sneakers.Children under 10 years old, people who are obese or too old, in my opinion, refrain.Once you reach the beach, it is a corner of paradise nestled between sea and cliffs.The waves are powerful. Swimming at our own risk (and peril).A must to do. One of the most beautiful beaches.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Touristy but definitely worth the descent
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Once you have left the hustle and bustle of the first steps behind you, the journey of discovery begins. During the department you regularly think about giving up. But once you're down you really have to admit that it was worth it. The climb up is tough but easier than down

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A must do
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Obviously a very touristy site but magnificent.Upstairs it’s packed with people and downstairs not at all.Of course the descent is not very easy but with good shoes and a little caution, it's okay because there are barriers on each side. The beach is very beautiful and the water too. You can buy a drink downstairs at a reasonable price (20,000 for a coke). Be careful of the waves, some of which are very powerful.For the climb back up, it’s hard but you can go slowly.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Time your trip
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A really nice view which makes for some great photos, especially on a nice day. Recommend coming here after 5pm once all the day trippers have gone. Lots of monkeys around too but they don’t seem to cause a problem.NB Parking scooter is 5,000 rupiah.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: nusa penida
reviewsWithKeywords.text: beautiful beach from above, even though it is very crowded with tourists and locals we still enjoy it, besides being so beautiful this place is also very clean

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great views, a little too crowded
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is probably, if not the most hyped place in Nusa Penida in particular and Bali in general. Having seen this particular sight multiple times in pics and videos across various platforms we were worried if it will impact our experience. Thankfully it didn't and there is nothing like viewing it yourself up close. We didn't go down to the beach but did enjoy the views from above and it is breathtaking to say the least. We reached around 10:30-11 am when it was too crowded. A must visit nonetheless!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: AMAZING
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Simply amazing! Kelingking is very much worth the trip, especially for the hike. It's not easy but it's worth it. I recommend to take your time there and assign a few hours for this locations. The beach is breathtaking.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Paradise in Bali
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nusa Penida is the biggest of the three Nusa islands just off from mainland Bali.Nusa Lembongan and Nusa Ceningan  make up the trio of islands,each with uniquely breath-taking landscapes. And has many tourist destinations that are very popular, one of the favorites is Kelingking Beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very beautiful landscapes!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I cant' explain how much I loved this place. I went to Nusa Penida island in January, just loved the landscape. Perfect destination for honeymoon couples. I visited 5 beaches there this one was the best. Broken beach is also a good option to visit.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: BE CAREFUL OF THE TIDE AT THE BEACH
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Me and my husband went to this view point in Nusa Penida today June 8th, 2023. A few minutes earlier, a couple died when they were dragged by the waves at the beach. I’m writing this to PLEASE ask anyone who visits this spot and decides to hike down to the beach to PLEASE not swim in the ocean. Especially if the locals tell you that the tide is high and it’s dangerous. There’s been A LOT of deaths and injuries in Nusa Penida which a lot of people don’t talk about. Please be careful. This is a beautiful place but you have to respect it and be extremely cautious.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Breathtaking
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Breathtakingly beautiful view. The steps are very steep and narrow, so beware before going down much as you have to climb back too. There are shops offering hats and food/beverages nearby. Go early in the morning for least crowds. Wear shoes.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: My Favourite of Penidas beaches
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We were a bit worried as the rain set in on our way up to the cliffs of Kelinking but as we reached the top the rain stopped and we had cool weather to tackle the stairs,We were there quite early so the crowds hadnt gathered and we had a clear walk down to take the photos.We didnt walk down to the beach as the stairs if you could call them that were steep and uneven.I liked the view from the top anyway.It is truely a beautiful site to behold and worth the uneven stairs.As the crowds began to gather we went to the left and there is a park where you pay 30000rph/pp to enter and take lots of touristy photos with different props and a stunning view of Kelinking from the right.Worth doing as well

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Breathtaking Spot
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Visit Nusa Penida island and travel to this beautiful breathtaking spot. You will get some astonishing views and will be able to click great pictures. Expect some crowd while visiting here. You will find some basic restaurants and shops near this location. Overall a must to visit the place.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful but very dangerous
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful but do NOT hike down in flip flops/sliders. Cannot believe how many people we saw risking their lives doing this. We wore trainers and it was a very strenuous hike/climb, literally rock climbing with your hands on the way back up.It is incredibly sweaty, incredibly steep and incredibly dangerous. Don't let the beautiful views deceive you.Once you clamber down to the bottom, the beach is beautiful and has a few vendors which are overpriced as expected. The waves are SO dangerous.It warms you not to go in the sea but so many people do. At times it was ok and we paddled in, then two of us got whacked by a huge wave and sucked under/out and spinning under the water. I genuinely feared for my life.So please only do this hike if you are fit, confident, have trainers, bring lots of water and stay out of the sea except to paddle in the edge, freak waves come at any moment and hit you/drag you out.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: View from the top
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It’s breathtaking from the top. We were there about 9:30am before the crowds - the only other crowds were monkeys! My husband and I began walking down. I consider myself fit, but had to turn back. The steep and narrow paths started to scare me plus it was very hot. My husband went further and got to the path leading  to the beach, but decided the risk wasn’t worth it as it looked too dangerous. When we came back up there were people everywhere and the path was getting so dangerously busy. Go early.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Words cannot describe how beautiful it is. It was worth to wait to our turn to take the picture. Everything was perfect!!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful view from the top!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful Beautiful Beautiful! Best to go very early in the morning to avoid the tourist crowds & tourist groups coming from Bali - if you go anytime after 10am you will be standing in long lines in the sun waiting to take a photo - it's beautiful and so worth seeing!You will have to be very fit to go down to the beach , it's a lot of steps and very steep - the view from the top is amazing and easily accessible.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: 2 adults and 10 year old - one adult made it down
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful from the top yea.Anyone wanna talk about the dangerous hike down? Steep block steps then it’s just chaos and actually dangerous. Nice to brag you were at the top though even if you didn’t finish the crazy hike.

reviewsWithKeywords.text: Visited on Feb 2023, weather was so sunny and everything was beautiful. The Nusa Penida island is so big and rough. We were in a ride of 40' from the port to get here and the roads were crazy but the beach is worth visiting.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great place to visit. Just wear comfy shoes
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Take a good pair of shoes and enjoy the hike down. Do not wear sandals or flip flops as it’s very difficult to descend down the cliff.  The hike down is not talked about enough. It’s very difficult to go down The beach at the bottoms is amazing to swim in. Worth a visit

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Exotic Kelingking !
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Kelingking - Exotic beach. Highly adventurous and one needs to be physically fit to descend the 400 meters (1312 Feet) steep cliff to enjoy the beach and then to climb back.  Not recommended if you are not physically fit. Wear good shoes, carry water bottles and don't forget to apply sun screen. It takes 30-40 minutes to descend and 40-50 minutes to climb back. waves are very forceful & rough. Be on guard if you get into sea. Plan well so that you are back before sunset.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: An instagramable moment - you’ll always cherish
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Kelingking Beach is arguably one of the most popular stops on Nusa Penida. It is located on the southwest coast of the island (about a 30-minute drive from Toya Pakeh Harbour). You have to pay a fee of 5,000 IDR for parking, which can be chaotic dependent upon how many other vehicles are there at the same time.It’s then about a five minute walk, along a well worn but rough path - which has a series of shacks, selling hats, food, coconuts and ice cream, to the coastal cliff.  The view from the top provides the most enchanting views of the island's coastline, where steep cliffs are greeted by crystal blue water. The safety at Kelingking is reliant on the bamboo railings. At many points along the cliff edge, there is no rail whatsoever and the grass just leads you off the edge, down hundreds of metres onto the rocks. A trip to Kelingking Beach can last anywhere from 10 minutes, if you are just there to take photos or have an Instagram moment, to over 3 hours, if you are up for the intense hike down (takes about 60 mins to get down to the beach and slightly longer to get back up). Whilst the beach looked so inviting the climb down and back looked exhausting. It is a spectacular view, which you share with hundreds of other tourists, but if you’ve travelled all the way to Nusa Penida then this is one of those iconic spots you need to visit.

reviewsWithKeywords.text: Kelingking Beach is the most beautiful spot of the trip to Bali. We did not go down far to the white sand beach because it would be dangerous for me and my boy. You can see mantas are playing from.The view from the viewpoint is absolutely stunning.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Kelingking Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Located in the south of Nusa Penida. This is a beautiful spot for photos and popular on instagram in the local search even worldwide search. The scenery is beautifull but too far away to climb down to the beach but the cliff is so beautifull to take some photos.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of a kind nature wonder
reviewsWithKeywords.text: As we arrived at Nusa Penida at 3 pm and had only one night there available, we had to choose only one point of interest to visit there. Our choice had turned to Kelingking Beach and, dear me, we made it right, as this place is something unbelievable! We had never seen such nature wonder in our lives, so we can safely say that tough road towards this place is absolutely worth it! We hadn’t gone down to the beach itself as we were said it could be dangerous, and since we had already had in our plans such adventurous undertaking as ascending to Mount Agung, so we decided not to take such a risk and enjoyed the view from above.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great place
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful place to visit, you can walk around and go downstairs to the beach, many monkeys around, be careful

I’m sure the view from the top is better than at the beach anyway.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The best way to work out! Amazing experience! Looking forward for the next round!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Well, I go to nusa penida island at lest 2-3 times per year with friends!So I will highly recommend you to rest before you go and have a good lunch!It will take a lot of time and effort to go down and back! I always enjoy it but Its not easy especially If not everyone in your group do work out every day ! So just get ready for people start crying!Its sunny so put some sun cream!  You can carry your water and etc but surprise surprise you can buy drinks by the beach too! Its soft drinks places so you can carry drinks or just some cash!Too about 1 hour down and back! Some people much longer!note: its no private or parking area so people just leave it anyhow! And its not easy to find this place so i will advice you to get a private guide! thats why my friends always asking me to join hahahaWe usually will racing with guys! Enjoy your day!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Hard to Get
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It is amazing panorama and worth to visit especially if you are a freak of landscape views. Reaching the beach which you have to hike down was challenging, unless you like hiking. I came here in the time in the sunset and able to enjoying the sun goes down form the cliff. The beach takes around 1 hour from the central, we went there with the motorcycle and witnesses the amazing views on the way to the beach

reviewsWithKeywords.title: pinkie finger beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Visited here last year in June,it is the landmark of Nusa Penida,kelingking means pinkie finger,the famous pic of this place is the cliff form in the shape of pinkie finger,thats why the local called it kelingking(pinkie),you will be exhausted if you want to go down to the beach.but it is worth doing so.once you reach the beach,you will feel so relaxed,and want to stay here longer.but the waves is strong,so not suitable for swimming. along the way to the beach, sometimes a bit dangerous,so take care of yourself.i should stay here longer, but sadly due to limited time,have to go up to meet my driver.will come again.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great View but difficult walk down the beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This place has absolutely great view. As this place is far,  I would advise to try hiring a driver instead of driving a scooter as this is the safest option. To see the  cliff with your own eyes and experience the height is absolutely worth it. Then we decided to go to beach so we can swim in beautiful blue sea and play in the white sand. Trail gets too steep and there are no longer steps, you are from that point on literally rock climbing down an almost upright cliff. Wearing a shoe for this hike is a must.  After finally reaching the bottom, it was all still beautiful, but the sea was also rough, high waves and strong tide, so it was hard to relax in the sea. In the beach there was only one small place selling some drinks and snacks. Overall, it was definitely very beautiful, the view and scene was amazing. The challenge is a bit hard but worth it and we all felt great after doing all this. I would give it 5 stars if only it was better maintained (stairs and facilities). Otherwise its beautiful.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice place
reviewsWithKeywords.text: there is a lot of walking to do here. but it still really amazing. At the time we went the place was quite crowded.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Perfect mix of beauty and adventure!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We arrived to Kelingking at around 8:00 in the morning to get a great start to the day (also because of the tide tables to maximize time on the beach!!!) We were one of two groups of people there and it was amazing (Keep in mind this was during the first ramp up of COVID-19 lockdowns, so our crowd experience is probably skewed). We sat at the top and took pictures for maybe 10 minutes with just us until the other couple and us started the hike down. The hike for experienced and sure-footed people can take around 20-25 minutes if you're not stopping along the way for pictures. We stopped for pictures and to help eachother with VERY steep parts of the hike down. As we got to the bottom, we saw the monkeys! They didn't mess with much of our things, but there was at least one person next to the bags and shoes the entire time because they initally ran right up to us and waited for us to leave something alone. The beach was perfect and tide was not too hard to swim against, The climb back up was where things started to take their toll. We stopped multiple times on the hike back up, (it didn't get less steep, and with us being wet and tired made the stops feel longer). By this time, other tourists were hiking down and the path isn't meant for that many people!! At one point we were still hanging on the rocks to let people through that were hiking down and clearly weren't prepared for an extensive, steep hike.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing views, worth the rocky journey!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the best spots in Nusa Penida. Amazing views, make sure to get there early. Luckily we got there around 10 am and there was no queue, only a few people walking up and down. Make sure to take some comfortable shoes. We took flip flops and we had to be very careful. If you are looking to go all the way down to the beach it will take you around 30/40 minutes so be prepared for the time of your life. The stairs going down are very narrow and you have to watch your step. The stairs are pretty crowded with people coming up and going down. If you are afraid of heights or if you don't have good balance I wouldn't recommend. This does require some level of fitness but once you get down, you will encounter the most amazing sand. Just watch out for the waves as they are very strong and they can pull you in. I would not recommend swimming in these waters. Perfect place for those Instagram pics!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Just wow! Amazing ❤
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Truly one of the most beautiful beaches I have seen. Looks amazing from the top, beautiful down the bottom. The beach is completely enclosed by high cliffs. The pathway down is extremely steep and rough. Don't even consider going down unless you are fit and agile. My family stayed up top to enjoy the amazing views while I went to the bottom. If you are brave  enough to reach the beach, it is definitely worth it! Beautiful water and sand, incredible scenery, could have stayed all day. Down wasn't hard for me, but the climb back up was tough. Loveliest beach on the island imo. Don't miss it.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wear sensible shoes
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Wonderful place! But come prepared. I've done the descent/climb two times now and I've seen a lot of people suffering needlessly because they went in flip-flops/barefoot. It can get pretty strenuous and the heat and the sun can get brutal. Also, waves get quite high and unpredictable. Swimming can be fun, but proceed with caution.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Majestic Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Kelingking beach definitely lived up to all the Instagram hype - this beach is unreal! From the cliffs overlooking the sea and the hike down to the beach, the views were something out of a movie.It gets quite warm and would recommend going early in the day to beat the crowds. Definitely worth the trip to Nusa Penida island!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Living T-rex
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Climb up a bit to the hill to get the full picture of this T-rex. There are some photo taking spot for you to take the best spot but you need to buy drinks or food to enter. Sadly you can see rubbish all around the bushes. Hopefully people who visit there or who ever run and taking care that places can be more aware about it.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Trash and crowd, that is was you get to see
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Was probably the most beautiful place in Nusa Penida back in time. Now it is a landfill with hordes of tourist. Thousand of empty plastic bottles along the way and once you get there, you almost wonder if you are at the shopping mall during the incredible sales day or if you are at the Kelingking Beach. People bumping into one each other, kids crying, adults fighting over a spot for photo, the worst of humanity is at Kelingking Beach.A tip: go down, way down, all the way down to escape this madness and rest on the beach sand. The way down is dangerous and hard, the way back up is even harder and you have to be in excellent physical condition. This limit the number of people going down and all of a sudden you can breath and see clear and enjoy what nature has to offer.On our way back up we decided to pick additional trash left by others to dispose properly. Please do same.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing view
reviewsWithKeywords.text: MUST visit to experience this amazing landscapes. May have a hard time on a speedy boat or using toilets in this island though.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning View
reviewsWithKeywords.text: So happy I did this, such amazing view like you see in movies, I could have stayed up there for hours relaxing.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Relaxing ! A cup of gelato won't hurt you.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The view from the view point is really cool. However, it would be better if I could go down the beach. You can actually. My travel agent said not enough time. I don't know how to explain it. It's a nice place to take a nap, windy, but not much to do or see. Get yourself a big cup of gelato ice cream around IDR50K. Why big? Because it melts faster. What I don't like about the place is you have to pay IDR5K for restroom. We deserve free public restroom.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sadly, it lost its beauty....
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Good: 1. Get a chance to see the most photographed beach in Nusa Penida2. Very accessible - no rough roads3. Great viewBad: I was year 3 years ago and it was different. Yes, there were huts (1-3) selling food and water but NOW?? There are around 10 huts selling stuff and trash everywhere. Sadly, it lost its beauty and aura.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Explorer
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Secluded, white sandy beach with turquoise waters enclosed by a steep cliff & headland... not easy to hike..

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Worth the hike. Some would disagree tho. You have to walk 600 steps (half of them rocks and not an easy way to get down) and then you have to walk it all up too! Definitely a challenge in the heat of the day even if you are in decent shape. But the views and experience are so worth it!!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous but a lot of tourists and trash
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One thing ticked off my bucket list. However be aware that there are a lot of tourists, trash and monkeys.BUTThe view is just as spectacular as in the photos.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Brave waves and beautiful view
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Amazing view, big waves, totally worth it, go early get down to the beach and stay there all day, there is enough shadow, enjoy the sea but carefully, bring a lot of water and something to eat!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Social Media Attraction
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The T Rex shaped cliff side at Kelingking Beach has rocketed tourism into the sky with its natural beauty. Thanks to social media, Instagram especially this viewpoint is now top of most people’s list of attractions when heading over Bali. The beach itself is secluded, white sandy haven surrounded by turquoise waters.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing place
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is very beautiful and the view is amazing...... .Recommended place. I will be come back again

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Take your best camera
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Worth the crowds, in my opinion. Go and take the pictures. I am in my 40s, don't take kindly to heat with hi humidity, and had an intense sunny hike the day before....so I did not climb down far enough to get to the craziest part of the climb down, BUT good news is, you can see how you feel and turn back whenever you think "none of these kids in flip flops will carry me back up, will they? Hm." Before you get to the super crazy part just know the stairs get steeper as you head down too.Conversely, you can get the higher views and head up... If you're taking each other's pics, watch your bags-- monkeys!  A few donation spots higher up as well where you can climb into platforms for pics. We saved our money for a cold drink!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Paradise is here
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Wire is amazing. It’s a bit hot here, but soooo beautiful. It’s so cool colors of water and nature. There is a lot of tourist and sometimes you have to wait for making a photo at popular points. You can go down to the beach, but it’s hard way.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The best place I've ever been
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This spot should be on everyone's bucketlist, I've never seen such a beauty, it's worth a one day visit.If you go there just be bold and do the hike (it's tiring but not dangerous)You should just mind to have a suitable footwear, sunscreen and a cap.Be careful ! if you drop your phone you'll never see it again 😂

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the most iconic beach in the world and no doubt why it is so. We visited this one our one day tour of Nusa Penida.Its nature's paradise.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A must stop in Nusa Penida
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Don't miss this outstanding place on Nusa Penida. If you choose to go all the way down to the beach just remember that what goes down must come up. It's not easy to get back up. If you plan to go down be sure to spend a couple of hours there. Beautiful views of the beach and surrounding cliffs. It does get very busy since all of the tours do make a stop at this beautiful place.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Absolutely beautiful, but busy.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is an absolutely gorgeous spot, the cliff and views are unbelievable.  That being said it was busy and we saw at least 3 people on our way down that looked like they were going to have heat stroke sitting on the stairs.  Stretch them legs and bring your sunscreen and lots of water!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful views
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Stunning views, can get very busy.We visited via a private tour using Warung Coconut, great value tour and extremely helpful guide.   It is quite a steep trek down to the actual beach if you decide to venture down.  The views from the cliffs above are absolutely beautiful.  There are a selection of cafe bars at the top.  Well worth a visit if you are on the island. The roads are very narrow to get there, so highly recommend using a private tour.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very beautiful beach! Bit challenging to get down to the beach and up again cause the path is not easy which makes it really crowded but worth climbing.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fantastic view
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The trip down and up is the main thing you will need to taka swim to cool down after the walk. Reserve enough time for this if you plan to go down to the beach

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Amazing view, not to much people ( low saison) You can even go down to the beach, but you need to be a good hiker 💪🏼

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very busy and dangerous if foolhardy
reviewsWithKeywords.text: When we were there it was unbelievably busy and people were standing right on the cliff edge taking selfies one hundred meters off the beach below. Totally crazy behavior. Spectacular views if you can avoid the crowds. Very steep and difficult access to the beach below where few people actually go.Mainly a viewpoint.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great view point
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Even though there’s heaps of people you can still find a spot for views and photos.The climb down to the beach is hilariously sketchy but good exercise and worth it for the crystal clear water swim below.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing view
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Consider twice if you want to go down the steps! Please mind the waves, they are fierce. There are many cafes are offering unhealthy food, but hey..  If you always eat healthy, maybe this is the time for french fries.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Only for advanced hikers
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nearly impossible to hike up and down safely given the steepness and jaggedness of the climb up and down . Yes the view from the top is stunning but do not attempt this hike unless you are very fit and wearing appropriate clothing. It gets more severe as you go down . You are crawling at some points. Uphill is worse and there are no danger signs. I read a lot of people have died here either from falling or drowning.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A selfie must have
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Yes, there are a lot of tourists here and yes, it would be great if there wasn't, but there's an obvious reason for that.To see the T-Rex cliff with your own eyes and experience the phenomenal hight is absolutely worth it.I didn't do anything but check the view, so I know nothing else about this place. All the pictures in the world can't do this place justice.If you are fit and in no fear of heights, you should definitely go down the steep stairs to the beach.You will be one of the few who has ever been down there.Here's a picture of Donny, the cool driver who made me scream and laugh at the same time, driving me to crazy places.. 😂For me, it was worth my time and I recommend going there.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Mesmerizing View
reviewsWithKeywords.text: When you arrive, you are going to be greeted with such amazing view of the entire place from above. Although it can get over exhausting to reach the beach below and back to the top. Worth the effort, never going down again though. Haha

Absolutely in love with this place. You can see from the top T-REX and Kelinking beach on the bottom. On the top was a lot of people, many tourist making photos. But you can climb stairs to the Kelingking beach, but it takes aroung 40 min. Be careful !Kelinking beach is really nice, small, white sand beautiful beach🌊It was my top place which i saw in our trip ☺️

reviewsWithKeywords.title: B E A U T I F U L!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The view itself is beautiful! But take the time to hike down to the beach. It's super steep but so worth it! You won't regret it! Go there late afternoon, less people and not too too hot! GO!!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: beautiful
