reviews.title: A very sad sight
reviews.text: The view is beautiful but at what price.You also have to look behind the scenes.It is so sad that a panoramic point is exploited in this way.Hundreds of scooters and cars parked a few hundred meters upstream.  Warong, shops of all kinds along the way. Hundreds of tourists playing neck and neck to get the best selfie. Plastic waste everywhere. Monkeys in the middle of all this garbage. reviews.title: A magical place despite some downsides
reviews.text: Kelingking Beach literally took our breath away. The panorama is amazingly beautiful: this cliff diving into a turquoise sea is simply unreal. The roads are frankly bumpy and tiring, and once you arrive, you have to deal with the crowds – even early in the morning, there are already a lot of people.What spoiled the magic a bit was the crane planted in the middle of the site, building an elevator. We understand the idea of facilitating access, but it distorts the landscape a little.Nevertheless, we have absolutely no regrets about our visit. It is a place to see at least once in your life.

reviews.title: A paradise that is shamefully coming to an end
reviews.text: We visited this amazing beach today. We arrived by scooter after about 50 minutes of winding narrow road and with many potholes. Parked the scooter (5,000 RP) we headed towards the view point which is definitely crowded but beautiful. We were prepared for the descent with hiking shoes and they are served. Guys it is a difficult and dangerous path, despite this we have seen people do it in slippers but with disproportionate difficulties. In some passages it is no longer even a trekking but a real climbing.  Once down the place is magical. A paradise that at the moment remains quite exclusive because 80% of tourists remain at the view point given the difficulties of the route and this is good to not see the beach invaded by “tourists” hunting for photos from social media. Unfortunately they are building a monstrous elevator to get everyone down and soon it will become a place annihilated by the masses. Embarrassing that the government allows these constructions with devastating environmental impact. On the other hand there is plastic and waste everywhere along the way. A people completely indifferent to the unprecedented ecological disaster of which they are the architects.

reviews.title: A Breathtaking Experience
reviews.text: Kelingking Beach is one of those places that actually lives up to the hype and then some. Seeing that iconic T-Rex-shaped cliff in person is surreal. reviews.title: Stunning, But Be Prepared For A Climb!
reviews.text: This beach is absolutely stunning, but you'll need sturdy shoes for the climb down and back up again. The steps are plentiful, steep, and rickety, so you'll need to be confident and fit to take them on. The view from the top, however, is undoubtedly one of the most beautiful imaginable and well worth the visit just for that.Also, the trip to this beach is something of an experience in itself, and it's VERY touristy. The roads on Nusa Penida are possibly the worst I've ever seen, but it's a scenic drive to the beach. Head down to the perfect beach, and you'll find you're pretty much alone to enjoy a swim in the picture-perfect sea.

reviews.title: Stunning, imposing and unmissable place.
reviews.text: An unforgettable experience! I recommend it to everyone who really likes to contemplate the beauty of nature. It's awesome! Standing up there on that cliff and seeing such infinity in front of you with an impressive set of mountains and a lonely beach, blows your mind. The road to get from the center of Nusa Penida on your own is very long and otherwise complicated. Now, though, is what I recommend you do.Renting a motorbike (which by the way cost very cheap and are in very good condition) and embarking on a trip barely dawns until you reach Kelingking Beach. It'll take you about an hour. It is a winding, dirt road and in some steep sections, but going slowly and with caution, nothing bad will happen to you.I clarify all this, because the other option to go, is with a tour. And I don't recommend that at all. Since when you arrive at the place, you will find it exploited with people, and the experience I assure you will be totally different than the one I tell you.As for the beach, you can go down on foot, but I didn't get to it. I stayed halfway as a precaution, took some pictures from a closer point and returned upstairs again. You have to be very well physically to be able to reach the beach, if or if with closed shoes and cap. At first, the descent is by means of a staircase made with the same stone of the mountain and with protection on the sides, but as the meters pass, it becomes more and more rustic, until it reaches the point where it is almost a crossing to be able to continue descending. In this part there is no protection at the sides and they offer only a thick rope (many years old) to assist you, but I recommend you to be very sure of what you will do since then you have to think that the same path you must do but in climb.I would definitely come back a hundred times more. If you're in Nusa Penida, you really can't miss it.PD: This section applies to all trips you make in Indonesia and especially if you visit this area: Be very careful with monkeys!

reviews.title: Gorgeous, not for snorkeling
reviews.text: This beach is gorgeous and if you’re in the area I highly recommend going at the start of the day because there are massive crowds otherwise. The trek down to the beach is for the brave and fit. Once you are past the trinket shops, there is no paved path. You literally hike down a very steep, narrow mountainside with poorly maintained handrails made of bamboo or trees. I also wouldn’t swim here and have no idea why any would recommend snorkeling. Maybe those who do went during a different time of year but be aware the surf and current is rough and not even the locals suggest swimming here. Absolutely stunning beach though please just be aware before you go.

reviews.title: Best vacation
reviews.text: My vacation to Bali and Nusa Penida was an unforgettable adventure. The natural beauty of Kelingking Beach and the surrounding areas left me in awe, and the sense of tranquility on the island was a welcome escape from the hustle and bustle of everyday life. While the island's infrastructure is still developing, its raw beauty and untouched landscapes make it a destination worth visiting.If you're planning a trip to Bali, I highly recommend adding Nusa Penida and Kelingking Beach to your itinerary. Just be prepared for a bit of adventure and a lot of walking - but trust me, it's all worth it!

reviews.title: Beautiful beach!
reviews.text: It offers some of the most amazing views in Bali and is well worth the effort to get there. Whether you’re hiking down to the beach for some solitude or simply taking in the scenery from the viewpoint, the experience is unforgettable.

reviews.title: Stunning rock formation
reviews.text: The Kelingking beach is about an hour's drive from the harbor. The roads to the harbor are narrow and broken at places, as are most roads in Nusa Penida. From the car park, there is a short walk through some shops to reach the path that leads down to the Beach.The views from the top of the cliff are stunning, and you can clearly make out the T-Rex rock formation. It's worth taking a lot of pictures from here. Watch out for monkeys though! There's a steep path leading down to the Beach—try this out only if you are really adventurous!There are a few stores selling souvenirs, water/juice, snacks, etc. There's also a money exchange outlet giving decent exchange rates.

reviews.title: beach
reviews.text: Visiting Kelingking Beach was an unforgettable experience. The breathtaking cliffside views, turquoise waters, and iconic T-Rex-shaped rock formation were absolutely stunning. The hike down was challenging but worth it for the pristine beach below. A true paradise!

reviews.title: Stunning Views and a Rewarding Hike – A Must-Visit at Kelingking Beach
reviews.text: Kelingking Beach is a true slice of paradise! The stunning cliffside view resembles a T-Rex, making it one of the most iconic spots in Bali. The turquoise water and pristine white sand are absolutely breathtaking. However, be prepared for a challenging hike down, as the path is steep and rocky. Once you reach the beach, you'll find it to be less crowded than other tourist spots, offering a peaceful retreat. The waves can be strong, so swimming is not always safe, but the scenery alone is worth the trip. Don’t forget to bring water and wear sturdy shoes!

reviews.title: Stunningly beautiful!

reviews.title: One of the best sites in the world
reviews.text: Make this your first stop when visiting Nusa Penida, and try to arrive early in the day. This is one of the most stunning locations in the world and a must-see for anyone visiting Bali. Only attempt the climb down if you're prepared for the challenging hike back up, as the ascent is steep and requires moderate trekking. Beyond a certain point, the stairs turn into uneven stones, making the climb even more difficult.

reviews.title: Magic view! Men..
reviews.text: We were two adults who made a day trip to Nusa Penida with 4 snorkeling stops and 4 stops on land. The boats in the morning came away later than expected in the end we only managed 1 stop on land and then we chose to visit Kelingking Beach. That beach was MAGICALLY nice, probably the finest we both saw. Nicer than all the beaches I've been to in Thailand. But what was sick was that there was a huge construction site and garbage pile and trash everywhere right next to the viewpoint where everyone took their pictures. It spoiled the feeling a bit but it is 100% worth a visit!

reviews.title: Kelingking Beach - Thrilling Road  and stunning view
reviews.text: The road to Kelingking Beach is notoriously difficult, especially for those not experienced with riding motorbikes. The winding, narrow paths, combined with poor road conditions, like potholes and sharp, unexpected turns, make it challenging to navigate. Many tourists rent motorbikes to get there, but the lack of experience with such tricky terrain can lead to accidents. It’s definitely important to be cautious and maybe even consider hiring a local driver if you’re not comfortable with those kinds of roads.After parking, paying the small fee, and you can leave your motorbike safely, you walk through the village to the iconic viewpoint. The climb down the hill to the beach starts there.There are monkeys along the village and view point. Monkeys are indeed quick and opportunistic! They might look harmless, but their behavior can change quickly when they sense food or anything resembling it. Keeping food securely packed and being mindful of your belongings is important, as they won’t hesitate to snatch anything they find interesting.The descent to Kelingking Beach is steep and physically demanding, so it’s important to be prepared. The climb down involves navigating rocky and narrow paths, and while going down may seem easier, the real challenge is the climb back up. It requires good physical fitness and stamina, especially under the heat. Bringing plenty of water is essential to stay hydrated, and having some prior physical training will definitely help with endurance.

reviews.text: Beautiful spot, were there by 9:30 a.m. so not too busy didn't walk all the way down as it was wet and would be too dangerous, pretty steep stairs, take walking shoes or walking sandals. we were lucky to see monkeys (don't put bag down). There's a great photo spot before you get to the stairs 50 meters or so on the right about a three minute walk across top.

reviews.title: Unbelievable Views at Kelingking Beach!
reviews.text: Kelingking Beach is nothing short of spectacular! The iconic T-Rex shaped cliff offers one of the most stunning views I’ve ever seen. The contrast between the turquoise waters, white sand, and lush greenery is simply breathtaking.Getting down to the beach is an adventure in itself—the hike is steep and challenging, but once you reach the bottom, it feels like you’ve discovered a hidden paradise. The beach is secluded, peaceful, and perfect for relaxing after the hike.Kelingking Beach is a must-see for anyone visiting Nusa Penida. The views alone are worth the trip, and the experience is one you’ll never forget. Highly recommended for anyone looking to experience the raw beauty of Bali!

reviews.title: Beautiful!!
reviews.text: This was truly an amazing experience! One of the most beautiful scenes we have seen in Bali! Gorgeous views and a stunning beach. There are lots of people, but the beach is huge so there’s plenty of room for pics alone. Just a PSA, the hike down is HARD!! Not sure if someone has mentioned this in reviews but we heavily underestimated how steep it is. Be prepared for a true climb during the last half to the beach. The way up is better but this really isn’t for kids or older adults. Get ready for a true workout! If you stay at the top, there are ample opportunities for photo ops but you can also go a little bit further down and take some good solo shots without all the crowd. I highly recommend this for anyone coming to Bali!

reviews.title: Kelingking Beach is the most gorgeous part of our trip to Bali.

reviews.title: Probably one of the most beautiful beaches in the world
reviews.text: Although I rate it five stars, I have mixed feelings when it comes to making the review. There are many people on the trail down to the beach.. it is not an easy path and you have to be a very agile person and go well equipped to do it without suffering. The problem is that there are a lot of people going down with flip-flops and without the physical capacity it requires, since the trail is practically dug into the rock and in some sections is literally vertical. If you get to the sand, it's a dangerous, hungover beach and nobody should take it as a joke. The week before our visit. A tourist drowned.

reviews.title: An amazing view!
reviews.text: The place is really amazing. Even if it is horribly touristic, the view is really unique! You can choose between admiring the view from above or going down to the beach. Warning: signs indicating that one descends “at our own risk” are not a joke: the descent is really dangerous, we did not expect such a level of difficulty. It starts with steps, then more steps and finally outright climbing, all along a cliff. And to get back on track, you have to have a real physical condition and especially good shoes (flip-flops, abstain!).About 45 minutes by scooter from Toyapakeh Harbour

reviews.title: Incredibly dangerous!!
reviews.text: Kelingking Beach offers beautiful views.But (!) it is overrun by many tourists and the path that leads down is insanely dangerous, steep and insufficiently secured. Unfortunately, a young man slipped before our eyes and fell straight into the depths. We're not sure he survived that deep fall. When you get to the bottom of the beach, the sun pops improbably hot. No wind blows through the bay. You should never cool down in the water, as the current can carry you away in a life-threatening way. Unfortunately, there is little warning about this. Great respect is required on the way back up. The path consists of stones and steep slopes and many of the visitors developed circulatory problems due to the steep climb and the sun. Please take good care when visiting this spot. We only recommend a view from above and definitely not walking down the path with children or just flip-flops.

reviews.title: You don't have to hurt yourself.
reviews.text: In fact, it looks exactly like the photos on the Internet. Unfortunately, it's completely overflowing. People over people. The access road is a disaster (unpaved, very deep potholes, totally unsuitable for cars and borderline for scooters). One wonders why the 50,000 per person to be paid by each tourist on arrival on the island do not go into such infrastructure. The construction work for the elevator down to the beach is already visible. Shame that nature will be destroyed and from next year the beach below will be completely overrun. Basically, the island was an absolute disappointment. Not designed for tourism, rip-off, completely overrated, see unfriendly people who only take, take, but take nothing for tourism.

reviews.title: Parking 5.000 rupees

reviews.title: Breathtaking
reviews.text: Stunning.A beautiful landscape.I explain below why I only gave 4 stars.Most people stop at the top of the steps, which is a shame, after which I can understand because the descent and ascent are very sporty.It starts with steps then it becomes climbing, so for adventurers remember to take suitable shoes, no sandals or taps, and especially do not be dizzy, do not forget to brush yourself with sunscreen.We went down with a 12 year old and a 9 year old girl (real chimpanzees), they had a lot of fun but the return was a bit trying for the girl, nevertheless she did!Downstairs, a beautiful beach, white sand and turquoise water, small cave and coconut trees to shelter from the sun.Watch out for the waves, swimming is a bit dangerous, the waves carry you away and they are powerful, we witnessed live an accident where a young lady dislocated her shoulder, she was rescued by boat.

reviews.title: Not bad
reviews.text: It’s a beautiful view and lookout location with monkeys nearby as well. The downside is the amount of people clamoring for that perfect IG shot. Also they’re in the process of building a glass elevator system that will take you directly down to the beach, ugh.

reviews.title: Beautiful but dangerous and strong waves!
reviews.text: This is indeed one of the most beautiful beach with blue water and golden sand. But, please be very very careful. Firstly, the hike up and down is tricky and dangerous. It's worth if you can do the climb and if you manage to hike down then be very very careful of the strong currents. DO NOT venture near the waters! Before going there, I saw number of videos and my only focus was on to the hike down and up. I was glad that we were able to get down and thought of enjoying the water. But, the waves were so strong that we fell in the water but managed to come out of the water but with difficulty. I wouldn't have gone near the water if I'd known about the strong wave situation before going or if there were any warnings signs (or may be I missed seeing the warning signs).Word of caution - Don't go near the water, its dangerous! Happy Travelling,PG

reviews.title: Stay Quiet and let beauty do the talking here.
reviews.text: The Kelingking Beach offers stunning panoramic views and crystal-clear turquoise waters. It's a popular spot for photography and hiking down to the beach. It’s unique cliff formation resembles the shape of a T-Rex dinosaur. This distinctive cliff has made the beach a popular spot for photography.The hike down the steep and rocky cliff to reach the beach is challenging. The hike takes around 30-40 minutes, but the stunning views along the way make it worth the effort. This is not for young children.Currents in the sea are strong and one has to be a very good swimmer to swim here. Great place in Bali that is simply wonderful to see.

reviews.title: Well worth the climb
reviews.text: You’ve all seen the views from the top but not that many people venture down to the beach. But you should do! Okay it looks like a scary climb but take it slowly and it’s actually much easier than it looks. The beach is simply lovely and as most people are scared by the climb it’s not that full. reviews.title: Important! Needs preparation, it's dangerous. Very beautiful
reviews.text: The most importantA very tough descent to the beach, at first there are normal steps, then there are vertical sections where you move like a rock climber. It’s realistic to pass for average physical training, with certain conditions1. Visiting time. Don't go after 11. It's unbearably hot, the descent takes 40-60 minutes. Narrow paths, part of the time you just stand, as people walk in both directions all day.I don’t see any point in going after 16. You can’t really see the sunset from the beach, the view is better from above, and getting back up is in the dark. We arrived at 8 am and spent the whole day there until 4 pm, this was the best option.2. What to take for the descent.- Good shoes are a must, ideally sneakers or sneakers; sandals are very dangerous. Since I was unprepared, it turned out to be easier to go down barefoot at the end. If you twist your ankle there, it’s unclear how they’ll get you out of there.- water- if you still go after 16, then a headlamp. There isn’t much of an option to hold a flashlight in your hands3. Waves on the beach. Be very careful. We were told that on this side of the island there are very treacherous currents and waves, you definitely can’t swim, people are jumping in the waves near the shore, I think it’s ok. There are several articles about those killed by the waves on this beach.4. What to eat on the beachThis is a very beautiful place. There are very few people in the morning, then there are more, but it’s quite comfortable. There is one “mini market”, bananas for 120 rubles each and other small expensive delights. We agreed back so that the guy from this store would carry all our things and we climbed lightlyOverall the place is amazing. And the feeling that you have overcome this steep descent adds some kind of pleasure to being there. It’s good if you have time to be there, I wouldn’t just go down to take a photo.

reviews.title: Kelingking Beach
reviews.text: Journey to the breathtaking Kelingking Beach, a hidden gem nestled in Nusa Penida, Indonesia. With its towering limestone cliffs and crystal-clear turquoise waters, this paradise offers an unforgettable escape. Explore pristine white sands, snorkel amidst vibrant marine life, or hike to the iconic T-Rex viewpoint for panoramic vistas. Surrender to nature's wonders at Kelingking Beach.

reviews.title: Serious physical training required!!!
reviews.text: First, the pros - this is truly one of the most beautiful beaches in the whole world - white soft sand, turquoise warm ocean, all surrounded by high mountains and greenery! There are almost no people (few people dare to descend). You rarely see such beauty. But for everything beautiful in this world you have to pay - I’m talking about the way down to the beach and back up. When I decided to descend, I read on several resources that “average physical fitness is required.” This is exactly what I have. BUT I want to warn many - visiting this beach requires much higher than average physical fitness! Comfortable shoes, water (at least 1.5 liters), and a hat are also required! Also calculate the time - the descent will take about 40/50 minutes, and the ascent will take more than an hour. Sometimes you need to climb almost a sheer cliff. There are huge waves on the beach - you also need to be very careful, since of course there are no lifeguards on site.

reviews.text: I really like this place because the view is very wild and many visitors who come here can also see the sunset

reviews.title: Beautiful View ... but unpleasant getting there
reviews.text: Beware - As stunningly beautiful this view and beach is, you need to consider whether it's worth the travel to get that 'Instagram' photo.Firstly, it's hazardous to those who wish to walk down the steep steps to the beach. Secondly, you can not swim on this beach as the currents are too strong, all the time.The view from the top is magnificent, but it's not a quick 5-minute car ride. Depending on where you are coming from or leaving from the Island, it's a 30 min + ride on terribly windy and narrow roads. This wasn't pleasant at all, and despite I've never got motion sickness, I felt unwell after this day trip.Many day tours from Bali (Sanur) offer snorkelling at Manta Bay, Gamat Bay, Wall Bay combined with lunch and 3 other land locations, including Kelinging Beach. This is way too much travelling for a day trip, and we even missed 2 locations due to running out of time. We left our accommodation at 7.30am and did not return until 6.00pm, that's fine, but the majority of that time was in transit, boat and car. I think if you were staying overnight on Nusa Penida, then a visit to Kelingking Beach viewpoint would be fine, but not during a day tour from Bali mainland. Trust me.

reviews.title: Amazing view

reviews.text: The view is just breathtaking,The most beautiful beach I have seen in my life.However, mass tourism spoils the beauty of the landscape.You cannot stay more than 5 minutes at the edge of the cliff to look at the view, because the Balinese ask you to get out of the frame to take photos for tourists! Impossible to take a step without stopping (so as not to interfere with a photo) because it's the place for Instagram! Tourists come in droves to take their photos then leave for the other known beaches of the island.

reviews.title: Stunning
reviews.text: The route to the destination is winding and steep the whole way, and it's not very wide. To navigate the course, Papasan automobiles must make turns. If you plan on going down, you should try to dress warmly and wear shoes and long trousers. The road features both stairs and sheer rocks at various points along its length. Take it slow and easy. Extremely difficult, but the exertion is worth it when you get to the beach at the bottom. Consider giving it a shot.

reviews.title: Best Beach in Bali
reviews.text: Outside of Bali, this is one of the most beautiful spots in the world. Every traveller ought to make a point of visiting Nusa Penida. Amazing locations on land and in the water to snorkel with manta rays and other marine life. The most enjoyable ones are Kelingking and Broken Beach.

reviews.title: Best View of Bali
reviews.text: Kelingking beach absolutely lived up to all of the hype that it received on Instagram; this beach is incredible. The views were like something out of a movie, both from the cliffs that looked out over the water and from the trail that led down to the beach. It can get fairly heated, so going early in the day is highly recommended if you want to avoid the crowds. The island of Nusa Penida is well worth the time and effort required to get there. If you want to get a better look at this T-rex, climb a little higher up on the hill. There are various photo shooting spots available for you to snap the greatest photos, but in order to access, you will need to purchase some refreshments or food first. Sadly, there is trash scattered throughout the bushes in every direction. We can only hope that those who go there and those who are responsible for running and maintaining those locations become more aware of it.

reviews.title: Sporty only if you want to go down
reviews.text: One of the most beautiful beaches in Indonesia, but it is earned with the sweat of your brow, not to mention your body. Good shoes and a bottle of water are essential. You are ready for an exceptional experience. Be careful of the current but swimming is essential to regain strength for the return. Don't embark on the adventure without good cardio but treat yourself to an unforgettable hike that will stand you out from the crowd. Beautiful solidarity of people taking the risk of adventure.

reviews.title: Must-see tourist spot
reviews.text: After paying just under 5k to park our scooter, we were given access to the viewpoint. You pass many shops and restaurants/warungs on the way up. Once at the top, the view is breathtaking. As breathtaking as the hordes of tourists who risk their lives for the perfect Instagram photo. Tip: Continue walking, past the descent and the viewing platform (each costing 5k) into the 'woods'. Walk as far as possible. After a 5-minute walk you are completely alone and you have a great view of one of the most famous spots in Bali. There is a lot of waste everywhere here. So do your part and just throw your waste in the bin.

reviews.title: Beautiful beach worth the climb, but be careful and don’t wear flip flops
reviews.text: We (a group of 8 friends) took a ferry from Serangan pier - it took about 1.5 h to Nusa penida and about 50 mins back. Then we rented scooters nearby and had a really nice drive to Kelingking beach. It was a nice view from the top, but looking down some of friends scared and didn’t want to go down to the beach (as 90 % of people) and one was scared of heights. Me and two friends went down anyway. The path is very very steep which makes it especially hard to walk/climb downhill. You sometimes have to wait for people going up as there is enough space only for one person on the path. You get dirty, dusty and scared for your life. However, when you come down it is totally worth it! The beach is not crowded, there is some nice shadow, you can buy some drinks and refresh in the sea (even though the current is too strong for swimming). Path down took us about 40 mins, but we were up in 20 - it is much easier to go up. If you only have limited time (one day trip) know that with hiking to the beach you will probably only have enough time to see this one beach (we were driving to Crystal bay afterwards but we only stayed there a couple of minutes - the beach is not as beautiful as Kelingking). Also on the way back the roads were crazy busy with cars and it was hard to ride the scooters. We managed to find one empty road so we could safely return to the pier. It was a fun trip overall :) Ps. Don’t wear flip flops or sandals for hiking to the beach! You will have to walk barefoot sooner or later. Bring sneakers.

reviews.title: Breathtaking view!
reviews.text: Great view! Get there early! From 8:30/9:00 a.m. onwards, lots of cars/scooters with tourists arrive! We didn't go down to the beach. The descent was very steep, some of the paths were unpaved. We saw manta rays from above! See picture 2.

reviews.title: Simply beautiful
reviews.text: During our visit to Nusa Penida we visited this beach. The landscape from the cliff is stunning... the rocks below seem to form a dolphin diving into a cobalt blue ocean. A perfect trip to this fabulous island...

reviews.title: The pearl of Nusa Penida
reviews.text: It truly is the pearl of Nusa Penida!Superb site, breathtaking view, a must.Going down the 150 meters is difficult and the climb back up even more, in some places it's climbing.To do early in the morning before the day tourists arrive or at the end of the afternoon when they are in the cars to reach their fast boat.Bring good shoes, forget the tones.

reviews.title: top location
reviews.text: One of the most beautiful places outside Bali. Only about 40 minutes boat ride from Sanur. Nusa Penida should be on every traveller's list. Amazing places to snorkel with Manta Rays and places to visit on land. Kelingking and Broken Beach are the best. Sexy Taxi Tours on Penida and Bob Marley is the best.

reviews.title: Beautiful, Breathtaking, Challenging!
reviews.text: The beach and the view is every bit beautiful as the pictures say. The way to get there is pretty challenging makes the beach the ultimate reward when you get there. Know your physical fitness, wear good shoes, climb slowly and carefully. take a liter of water in your backpack. The water was perfect, it was a little rough. Great photo opportunities. The hike down is 25 mins and the hike up is another 40 mins. The hike up is definitely really difficult and will test your physical fitness.

reviews.title: Gorgeous
reviews.text: Quite unique as a place of great beauty, access down to the beach difficult to access, very steep descent and many people count 40 minutes for the descent but it is worth it

reviews.title: Magnificent to see absolutely….
reviews.text: It’s a must-see place to do when you go to Bali and more particularly to Nusa PENIDA. The place is exceptional. We made the descent and frankly it was worth it. It’s physical and at times dangerous for some people, but when you get to the bottom: WOW, it’s GREAT. Allow around 1h30 down and up with more or less traffic.

reviews.title: Amazing
reviews.text: Very beautiful beach, I didn't go down because I was very sporty. I went there in the morning with a guide (13€) to visit the surrounding area on a scooter. At the end of September and early in the morning there were not too many people.

reviews.title: Beautiful cliff and beach in Nusa Penida
reviews.text: Superb beach in Nusa Penida! Lots of people, but worth it. The descent is a bit difficult, but the beach is magnificent. Parking costs 5000 rupees and there are food options on site. I insist on taking sports shoes to make it easier for you to get down and back up and not to hurt yourself 🫶🏼☀️

reviews.title: Dangerous access to the beach.
reviews.text: No beach is worth taking such risks.Access to the beach is very dangerous. No indications or access limitations.Especially not to do with young children or if you are not in very good physical condition.In short, don't go there.

reviews.title: The view is immaculate
reviews.text: Memorable view. I didn’t walk down the stairs as I already had at diamond beach that day. Not a swimmable beach as sea current is far too strong and will have you swept away in seconds unable to reach back to the beach.

reviews.title: Lovely views
reviews.text: A place worth seeing. Beautiful views. As the main attraction of Nusa Penida, it is visited by crowds of tourists every day. There are big traffic jams on the way there because the roads are in terrible condition and very narrow. Parking is cheap but often crowded. Going to the beach requires a lot of effort and is not easy. You can meet monkeys on the mountain.

reviews.title: A mandatory stop if u are in Nusa Penida
reviews.text: We, a family with one 7 year kid spent not more than 40 mins here. The view of the beach is breathtaking. There was a small contention for the photo spots. After that, we took some photos. But, the spots have very weak fences. One has to be very mindful of the same.

reviews.title: Climbing down is a memorable experience!
reviews.text: A stunning beach and a memorable experience climbing down to it. Yes, it’s tough, wear trainers, don’t carry anything unless it’s on your back and bring water. Harder than I imagined and my legs ached for days, but what an achievement when you reach the bottom! The steps end about a third of the way down, then it’s just rock climbing , so if you find the steps tough then turn back!

reviews.title: Recommended to get up early 🤓
reviews.text: We went today. At 8 in the morning we were there and there were almost no people, no lines or anything. The views from above are already worth it. It is spectacular! We have gone down, the descent is a bit peculiar since you cannot go super fast either with flip flops or barefoot. You have to go with sneakers and there is no problem, it is not as complicated as they say, you just have to go little by little and holding on to a railing. It is true that it is not suitable for 100% of the population and that is why I do not give it the highest score.I put on a tracksuit to go down because I knew it was going to get dirty and indeed the black hands on the reed railing and the railing need to be grabbed, otherwise it is impossible to go down or up. It took us about 25 minutes to go down. There are a lot of waves down there, you can't swim as such because it's quite dangerous but it's worth going down. Below you can buy pringles, coconuts, drinks...The climb is more tiring, you have to hold onto some ropes and the railings. It took us 25 minutes to go up, stopping occasionally because people were getting off but not many. When we went up it would have been 10 or something and there were already all the lines, a lot of people and a lot of people arriving. We stayed in Nusa Penida for 5 nights, although it is worth staying some day to be able to go early because it has nothing to do with it 😊

reviews.title: L’Époustouflante is worth it!
reviews.text: A panorama, a beach, water, waves… breathtaking!!!This beach is by far the number 1 on the island.Unfortunately terribly busy which makes its access even more sporty (and long)From the top of the cliff the view of the beach is incredible! Harmony of color, perfection of nature.To reach 200 m further down you have to take a staircase, first concreted, then a steep and very narrow path which ends almost in climbing mode. With the flow, allow 30 minutes to go down and 20 to go up. It’s quite physical because it’s very steep, all in the Indonesian heat!Bring water and a pair of sneakers.Children under 10 years old, people who are obese or too old, in my opinion, refrain.Once you reach the beach, it is a corner of paradise nestled between sea and cliffs.The waves are powerful. Swimming at our own risk (and peril).A must to do. One of the most beautiful beaches.

reviews.title: Touristy but definitely worth the descent
reviews.text: Once you have left the hustle and bustle of the first steps behind you, the journey of discovery begins. During the department you regularly think about giving up. But once you're down you really have to admit that it was worth it. The climb up is tough but easier than down

reviews.title: A must do
reviews.text: Obviously a very touristy site but magnificent.Upstairs it’s packed with people and downstairs not at all.Of course the descent is not very easy but with good shoes and a little caution, it's okay because there are barriers on each side. The beach is very beautiful and the water too. You can buy a drink downstairs at a reasonable price (20,000 for a coke). Be careful of the waves, some of which are very powerful.For the climb back up, it’s hard but you can go slowly.

reviews.title: Time your trip
reviews.text: A really nice view which makes for some great photos, especially on a nice day. Recommend coming here after 5pm once all the day trippers have gone. Lots of monkeys around too but they don’t seem to cause a problem.NB Parking scooter is 5,000 rupiah.

reviews.title: Paradise in Bali
reviews.text: Nusa Penida is the biggest of the three Nusa islands just off from mainland Bali.Nusa Lembongan and Nusa Ceningan  make up the trio of islands,each with uniquely breath-taking landscapes. And has many tourist destinations that are very popular, one of the favorites is Kelingking Beach.

reviews.title: Very beautiful landscapes!
reviews.text: I cant' explain how much I loved this place. I went to Nusa Penida island in January, just loved the landscape. Perfect destination for honeymoon couples. I visited 5 beaches there this one was the best. Broken beach is also a good option to visit.

reviews.title: BE CAREFUL OF THE TIDE AT THE BEACH
reviews.text: Me and my husband went to this view point in Nusa Penida today June 8th, 2023. A few minutes earlier, a couple died when they were dragged by the waves at the beach. I’m writing this to PLEASE ask anyone who visits this spot and decides to hike down to the beach to PLEASE not swim in the ocean. Especially if the locals tell you that the tide is high and it’s dangerous. There’s been A LOT of deaths and injuries in Nusa Penida which a lot of people don’t talk about. Please be careful. This is a beautiful place but you have to respect it and be extremely cautious.

reviews.title: A must visit
reviews.text: Without doubt the number 1 natural landscape attraction on Nusa Penida. Every tour operator comes here hence always plenty of visitors. Souvenir and food shops around the top area as well as a monkey or two so be mindful of your belongings.It is a steep descent via the steps to the beach so you need a good level of fitness in your legs as you have to come all the way back up. At my age I was happy to have my driver take some selfies of me.

reviews.title: Breathtaking
reviews.text: Breathtakingly beautiful view. The steps are very steep and narrow, so beware before going down much as you have to climb back too. There are shops offering hats and food/beverages nearby. Go early in the morning for least crowds. Wear shoes.

reviews.title: My Favourite of Penidas beaches
reviews.text: We were a bit worried as the rain set in on our way up to the cliffs of Kelinking but as we reached the top the rain stopped and we had cool weather to tackle the stairs,We were there quite early so the crowds hadnt gathered and we had a clear walk down to take the photos.We didnt walk down to the beach as the stairs if you could call them that were steep and uneven.I liked the view from the top anyway.It is truely a beautiful site to behold and worth the uneven stairs.As the crowds began to gather we went to the left and there is a park where you pay 30000rph/pp to enter and take lots of touristy photos with different props and a stunning view of Kelinking from the right.Worth doing as well

reviews.title: Breathtaking Spot
reviews.text: Visit Nusa Penida island and travel to this beautiful breathtaking spot. You will get some astonishing views and will be able to click great pictures. Expect some crowd while visiting here. You will find some basic restaurants and shops near this location. Overall a must to visit the place.

reviews.title: Beautiful but very dangerous
reviews.text: Beautiful but do NOT hike down in flip flops/sliders. Cannot believe how many people we saw risking their lives doing this. We wore trainers and it was a very strenuous hike/climb, literally rock climbing with your hands on the way back up.It is incredibly sweaty, incredibly steep and incredibly dangerous. Don't let the beautiful views deceive you.Once you clamber down to the bottom, the beach is beautiful and has a few vendors which are overpriced as expected. The waves are SO dangerous.It warms you not to go in the sea but so many people do. At times it was ok and we paddled in, then two of us got whacked by a huge wave and sucked under/out and spinning under the water. I genuinely feared for my life.So please only do this hike if you are fit, confident, have trainers, bring lots of water and stay out of the sea except to paddle in the edge, freak waves come at any moment and hit you/drag you out.

I consider myself fit, but had to turn back. The steep and narrow paths started to scare me plus it was very hot. My husband went further and got to the path leading  to the beach, but decided the risk wasn’t worth it as it looked too dangerous. When we came back up there were people everywhere and the path was getting so dangerously busy. Go early.

reviews.title: Exotic Kelingking !
reviews.text: Kelingking - Exotic beach. Highly adventurous and one needs to be physically fit to descend the 400 meters (1312 Feet) steep cliff to enjoy the beach and then to climb back.  Not recommended if you are not physically fit. Wear good shoes, carry water bottles and don't forget to apply sun screen. It takes 30-40 minutes to descend and 40-50 minutes to climb back. waves are very forceful & rough. Be on guard if you get into sea. Plan well so that you are back before sunset.

reviews.title: An instagramable moment - you’ll always cherish
reviews.text: Kelingking Beach is arguably one of the most popular stops on Nusa Penida. It is located on the southwest coast of the island (about a 30-minute drive from Toya Pakeh Harbour). You have to pay a fee of 5,000 IDR for parking, which can be chaotic dependent upon how many other vehicles are there at the same time.It’s then about a five minute walk, along a well worn but rough path - which has a series of shacks, selling hats, food, coconuts and ice cream, to the coastal cliff.  The view from the top provides the most enchanting views of the island's coastline, where steep cliffs are greeted by crystal blue water. The safety at Kelingking is reliant on the bamboo railings. At many points along the cliff edge, there is no rail whatsoever and the grass just leads you off the edge, down hundreds of metres onto the rocks. A trip to Kelingking Beach can last anywhere from 10 minutes, if you are just there to take photos or have an Instagram moment, to over 3 hours, if you are up for the intense hike down (takes about 60 mins to get down to the beach and slightly longer to get back up). Whilst the beach looked so inviting the climb down and back looked exhausting. It is a spectacular view, which you share with hundreds of other tourists, but if you’ve travelled all the way to Nusa Penida then this is one of those iconic spots you need to visit.

The beach takes around 1 hour from the central, we went there with the motorcycle and witnesses the amazing views on the way to the beach

reviews.title: pinkie finger beach
reviews.text: Visited here last year in June,it is the landmark of Nusa Penida,kelingking means pinkie finger,the famous pic of this place is the cliff form in the shape of pinkie finger,thats why the local called it kelingking(pinkie),you will be exhausted if you want to go down to the beach.but it is worth doing so.once you reach the beach,you will feel so relaxed,and want to stay here longer.but the waves is strong,so not suitable for swimming. along the way to the beach, sometimes a bit dangerous,so take care of yourself.i should stay here longer, but sadly due to limited time,have to go up to meet my driver.will come again.

reviews.title: Great View but difficult walk down the beach
reviews.text: This place has absolutely great view. As this place is far,  I would advise to try hiring a driver instead of driving a scooter as this is the safest option. To see the  cliff with your own eyes and experience the height is absolutely worth it. Then we decided to go to beach so we can swim in beautiful blue sea and play in the white sand. Trail gets too steep and there are no longer steps, you are from that point on literally rock climbing down an almost upright cliff. Wearing a shoe for this hike is a must.  After finally reaching the bottom, it was all still beautiful, but the sea was also rough, high waves and strong tide, so it was hard to relax in the sea. In the beach there was only one small place selling some drinks and snacks. Overall, it was definitely very beautiful, the view and scene was amazing. The challenge is a bit hard but worth it and we all felt great after doing all this. I would give it 5 stars if only it was better maintained (stairs and facilities). Otherwise its beautiful.

reviews.title: Nice place
reviews.text: there is a lot of walking to do here. but it still really amazing. At the time we went the place was quite crowded.

reviews.title: Perfect mix of beauty and adventure!
reviews.text: We arrived to Kelingking at around 8:00 in the morning to get a great start to the day (also because of the tide tables to maximize time on the beach!!!) We were one of two groups of people there and it was amazing (Keep in mind this was during the first ramp up of COVID-19 lockdowns, so our crowd experience is probably skewed). We sat at the top and took pictures for maybe 10 minutes with just us until the other couple and us started the hike down. The hike for experienced and sure-footed people can take around 20-25 minutes if you're not stopping along the way for pictures. We stopped for pictures and to help eachother with VERY steep parts of the hike down. As we got to the bottom, we saw the monkeys! They didn't mess with much of our things, but there was at least one person next to the bags and shoes the entire time because they initally ran right up to us and waited for us to leave something alone. The beach was perfect and tide was not too hard to swim against, The climb back up was where things started to take their toll. We stopped multiple times on the hike back up, (it didn't get less steep, and with us being wet and tired made the stops feel longer). By this time, other tourists were hiking down and the path isn't meant for that many people!! At one point we were still hanging on the rocks to let people through that were hiking down and clearly weren't prepared for an extensive, steep hike.

reviews.title: Amazing views, worth the rocky journey!
reviews.text: One of the best spots in Nusa Penida. Amazing views, make sure to get there early. Luckily we got there around 10 am and there was no queue, only a few people walking up and down. Make sure to take some comfortable shoes. We took flip flops and we had to be very careful. If you are looking to go all the way down to the beach it will take you around 30/40 minutes so be prepared for the time of your life. The stairs going down are very narrow and you have to watch your step. The stairs are pretty crowded with people coming up and going down. If you are afraid of heights or if you don't have good balance I wouldn't recommend. This does require some level of fitness but once you get down, you will encounter the most amazing sand. Just watch out for the waves as they are very strong and they can pull you in. I would not recommend swimming in these waters. Perfect place for those Instagram pics!

reviews.title: Just wow! Amazing ❤
reviews.text: Truly one of the most beautiful beaches I have seen. Looks amazing from the top, beautiful down the bottom. The beach is completely enclosed by high cliffs. The pathway down is extremely steep and rough. Don't even consider going down unless you are fit and agile. My family stayed up top to enjoy the amazing views while I went to the bottom. If you are brave  enough to reach the beach, it is definitely worth it! Beautiful water and sand, incredible scenery, could have stayed all day. Down wasn't hard for me, but the climb back up was tough. Loveliest beach on the island imo. Don't miss it.

reviews.title: Wear sensible shoes
reviews.text: Wonderful place! But come prepared. I've done the descent/climb two times now and I've seen a lot of people suffering needlessly because they went in flip-flops/barefoot. It can get pretty strenuous and the heat and the sun can get brutal. Also, waves get quite high and unpredictable. Swimming can be fun, but proceed with caution.

reviews.title: Majestic Beach
reviews.text: Kelingking beach definitely lived up to all the Instagram hype - this beach is unreal! From the cliffs overlooking the sea and the hike down to the beach, the views were something out of a movie.It gets quite warm and would recommend going early in the day to beat the crowds. Definitely worth the trip to Nusa Penida island!!

reviews.title: Living T-rex
reviews.text: Climb up a bit to the hill to get the full picture of this T-rex. There are some photo taking spot for you to take the best spot but you need to buy drinks or food to enter. Sadly you can see rubbish all around the bushes. Hopefully people who visit there or who ever run and taking care that places can be more aware about it.

reviews.title: Picturesque scenery!
reviews.text: Wonderful scenery. You can just stay on top and enjoy the sunset. Or hike down to beach for a dip. The hike up and down to Kelingking beach is good cardio workout...At least put on a proper sandal because the trail down is quite slippery...

reviews.title: Trash and crowd, that is was you get to see
reviews.text: Was probably the most beautiful place in Nusa Penida back in time. Now it is a landfill with hordes of tourist. Thousand of empty plastic bottles along the way and once you get there, you almost wonder if you are at the shopping mall during the incredible sales day or if you are at the Kelingking Beach. People bumping into one each other, kids crying, adults fighting over a spot for photo, the worst of humanity is at Kelingking Beach.A tip: go down, way down, all the way down to escape this madness and rest on the beach sand. The way down is dangerous and hard, the way back up is even harder and you have to be in excellent physical condition. This limit the number of people going down and all of a sudden you can breath and see clear and enjoy what nature has to offer.On our way back up we decided to pick additional trash left by others to dispose properly. Please do same.

reviews.title: Amazing view
reviews.text: MUST visit to experience this amazing landscapes. May have a hard time on a speedy boat or using toilets in this island though.

reviews.title: Stunning View
reviews.text: So happy I did this, such amazing view like you see in movies, I could have stayed up there for hours relaxing.

reviews.title: Relaxing ! A cup of gelato won't hurt you.
reviews.text: The view from the view point is really cool. However, it would be better if I could go down the beach. You can actually. My travel agent said not enough time. I don't know how to explain it. It's a nice place to take a nap, windy, but not much to do or see. Get yourself a big cup of gelato ice cream around IDR50K. Why big? Because it melts faster. What I don't like about the place is you have to pay IDR5K for restroom. We deserve free public restroom.

reviews.title: Sadly, it lost its beauty....
reviews.text: Good: 1. Get a chance to see the most photographed beach in Nusa Penida2. Very accessible - no rough roads3. Great viewBad: I was year 3 years ago and it was different. Yes, there were huts (1-3) selling food and water but NOW?? There are around 10 huts selling stuff and trash everywhere. Sadly, it lost its beauty and aura.

reviews.title: Explorer
reviews.text: Secluded, white sandy beach with turquoise waters enclosed by a steep cliff & headland... not easy to hike..

reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.text: Worth the hike. Some would disagree tho. You have to walk 600 steps (half of them rocks and not an easy way to get down) and then you have to walk it all up too! Definitely a challenge in the heat of the day even if you are in decent shape. But the views and experience are so worth it!!!

reviews.title: Gorgeous but a lot of tourists and trash
reviews.text: One thing ticked off my bucket list. However be aware that there are a lot of tourists, trash and monkeys.BUTThe view is just as spectacular as in the photos.

reviews.title: Brave waves and beautiful view
reviews.text: Amazing view, big waves, totally worth it, go early get down to the beach and stay there all day, there is enough shadow, enjoy the sea but carefully, bring a lot of water and something to eat!

reviews.title: Social Media Attraction
reviews.text: The T Rex shaped cliff side at Kelingking Beach has rocketed tourism into the sky with its natural beauty. Thanks to social media, Instagram especially this viewpoint is now top of most people’s list of attractions when heading over Bali. The beach itself is secluded, white sandy haven surrounded by turquoise waters.

reviews.title: Amazing place
reviews.text: The beach is very beautiful and the view is amazing...... .Recommended place. I will be come back again

reviews.title: Take your best camera
reviews.text: Worth the crowds, in my opinion. Go and take the pictures. I am in my 40s, don't take kindly to heat with hi humidity, and had an intense sunny hike the day before....so I did not climb down far enough to get to the craziest part of the climb down, BUT good news is, you can see how you feel and turn back whenever you think "none of these kids in flip flops will carry me back up, will they? Hm." Before you get to the super crazy part just know the stairs get steeper as you head down too.Conversely, you can get the higher views and head up... If you're taking each other's pics, watch your bags-- monkeys!  A few donation spots higher up as well where you can climb into platforms for pics. We saved our money for a cold drink!

reviews.title: Must Visit
reviews.text: This one the most craziest place ever i have visited. You must be there and take pictures and enjoy the beauty of nature. Must must must Go

reviews.title: Paradise is here
reviews.text: Wire is amazing. It’s a bit hot here, but soooo beautiful. It’s so cool colors of water and nature. There is a lot of tourist and sometimes you have to wait for making a photo at popular points. You can go down to the beach, but it’s hard way.

reviews.title: The best place I've ever been
reviews.text: This spot should be on everyone's bucketlist, I've never seen such a beauty, it's worth a one day visit.If you go there just be bold and do the hike (it's tiring but not dangerous)You should just mind to have a suitable footwear, sunscreen and a cap.Be careful ! if you drop your phone you'll never see it again 😂

reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.text: One of the most iconic beach in the world and no doubt why it is so. We visited this one our one day tour of Nusa Penida.Its nature's paradise.

reviews.title: A must stop in Nusa Penida
reviews.text: Don't miss this outstanding place on Nusa Penida. If you choose to go all the way down to the beach just remember that what goes down must come up. It's not easy to get back up. If you plan to go down be sure to spend a couple of hours there. Beautiful views of the beach and surrounding cliffs. It does get very busy since all of the tours do make a stop at this beautiful place.

reviews.title: Absolutely beautiful, but busy.
reviews.text: This is an absolutely gorgeous spot, the cliff and views are unbelievable.  That being said it was busy and we saw at least 3 people on our way down that looked like they were going to have heat stroke sitting on the stairs.  Stretch them legs and bring your sunscreen and lots of water!

reviews.title: Beautiful views
reviews.text: Stunning views, can get very busy.We visited via a private tour using Warung Coconut, great value tour and extremely helpful guide.   It is quite a steep trek down to the actual beach if you decide to venture down.  The views from the cliffs above are absolutely beautiful.  There are a selection of cafe bars at the top.  Well worth a visit if you are on the island. The roads are very narrow to get there, so highly recommend using a private tour.

reviews.title: Beautiful beach
reviews.text: Very beautiful beach! Bit challenging to get down to the beach and up again cause the path is not easy which makes it really crowded but worth climbing.

reviews.title: Fantastic view
reviews.text: The trip down and up is the main thing you will need to taka swim to cool down after the walk. Reserve enough time for this if you plan to go down to the beach

reviews.title: Guiding My Client at Kelingking Clift Beach
reviews.text: Nusa Penida it,s the best place to visiting. Beautufull panorama beach make every tourist will be come back again. You can going by Fast Boat Cruises 40 minuts from Sanur harbour. One day for visiting many place at Nusa Penida its our service.

reviews.title: Amazing
reviews.text: Amazing view, not to much people ( low saison) You can even go down to the beach, but you need to be a good hiker 💪🏼

reviews.title: Very busy and dangerous if foolhardy
reviews.text: When we were there it was unbelievably busy and people were standing right on the cliff edge taking selfies one hundred meters off the beach below. Totally crazy behavior. Spectacular views if you can avoid the crowds. Very steep and difficult access to the beach below where few people actually go.Mainly a viewpoint.

reviews.title: Great view point
reviews.text: Even though there’s heaps of people you can still find a spot for views and photos.The climb down to the beach is hilariously sketchy but good exercise and worth it for the crystal clear water swim below.

reviews.title: Amazing view
reviews.text: Consider twice if you want to go down the steps! Please mind the waves, they are fierce. There are many cafes are offering unhealthy food, but hey..  If you always eat healthy, maybe this is the time for french fries.

reviews.title: Only for advanced hikers
reviews.text: Nearly impossible to hike up and down safely given the steepness and jaggedness of the climb up and down . Yes the view from the top is stunning but do not attempt this hike unless you are very fit and wearing appropriate clothing. It gets more severe as you go down . You are crawling at some points. Uphill is worse and there are no danger signs. I read a lot of people have died here either from falling or drowning.

reviews.title: A selfie must have
reviews.text: Yes, there are a lot of tourists here and yes, it would be great if there wasn't, but there's an obvious reason for that.To see the T-Rex cliff with your own eyes and experience the phenomenal hight is absolutely worth it.I didn't do anything but check the view, so I know nothing else about this place. All the pictures in the world can't do this place justice.If you are fit and in no fear of heights, you should definitely go down the steep stairs to the beach.You will be one of the few who has ever been down there.Here's a picture of Donny, the cool driver who made me scream and laugh at the same time, driving me to crazy places.. 😂For me, it was worth my time and I recommend going there.

reviews.title: Great view!
reviews.text: I really love this beach especially if it could be a little bit quite. It is really worth to go down and do the trekking, it was like a treasure for me.

reviews.title: Mesmerizing View
reviews.text: When you arrive, you are going to be greeted with such amazing view of the entire place from above. Although it can get over exhausting to reach the beach below and back to the top. Worth the effort, never going down again though. Haha

Absolutely in love with this place. You can see from the top T-REX and Kelinking beach on the bottom. On the top was a lot of people, many tourist making photos. But you can climb stairs to the Kelingking beach, but it takes aroung 40 min. Be careful !Kelinking beach is really nice, small, white sand beautiful beach🌊It was my top place which i saw in our trip ☺️

reviews.title: B E A U T I F U L!
reviews.text: The view itself is beautiful! But take the time to hike down to the beach. It's super steep but so worth it! You won't regret it! Go there late afternoon, less people and not too too hot! GO!!!

reviews.title: beautiful
reviews.text: We went there in the afternoon so it was super hot. Better to go in the morning or in the afternoon i think.Next visit i would like to climb down the white sandy beach.

reviews.title: Sunset @KelingkingBeach
reviews.text: the best time to visit is in the afternoon, the less crowd, the best time to enjoy the scenery especially the sunset

reviews.title: T-Rex!
reviews.text: This is the best and most famous spot in Nusa Penida. Nusa Penida can be reached by boat from Sanur Beach Harbour in 1 hour. From Buyuk Harbour in Nusa Penida, Kelingking Beach is around 30 minutes by car. From the car park we must take a walk for around 100 m. There are some viewing spots. Try all to take best picture from several angles.In holiday season this spot is very crowded. And in December also very hot.The very unique is the shape of the cape looks like t-rex head.

reviews.title: Get there early
reviews.text: Always a great spot but has become a tourist Mecca in the last couple of years. It’s as good as the Instagram pics but get there early before the dayboats arrive. It gets hectic after 9am. Watch the monkeys too. No eye contact or they’ll go you. Our second visit and no doubt not our last. Will aim for sunset next trip.

reviews.title: Breathtaking!!!
reviews.text: The Views, awesomeThe landscape, stunningA bit of traffic going there since the streets can get very narrow.  Once there the crowd does make one a bit anxious as the first few photo opps along the stairs too are narrow.  But chill enjoy take a deep breath it’s lovely.If you wish to take the harrowing journey all the way to the beach, you really should be in good condition.  Strong legs, good knees and such.Despite some drawbacks, it’s worth the view!

reviews.title: Top of the top in Indonesia
reviews.text: Totally amazing place. A lot of people like in every tourist places. I recommend go there as earlier you can.

reviews.title: Best spot for taking pic in this island
reviews.text: However, its totally overcrowded. Also there is very hot, so we didnt hike down... it wud have been noce to swim there 🙂But view is nice, it was worth the visit.

reviews.title: Great spot for pic
reviews.text: This place is famous for the instagram-worthy picture and expects more crowd. We went there on Friday around 12pm. The place is crowded with China tourists. You have to walk around 5-8mins from carpark area to the Kelingking Beach entrance aka stairs. The stairs are quite narrow, ground not even (mud surface) and the hand rails are made from trees branches. Must be extra careful when you walk down the stairs & not to fall down because the side is high cliffs. We didn't walk all the way down because our driver said it's quite long way to hike down to the beach and bit dangerous for us. So we only stop half way and spot few picturesque views to take pictures. You might need to queue up at famous photo spot. Overall, we take around 40mins at that place.

reviews.title: Gorgeous
reviews.text: Beautiful! This place is spectacular. The steps down to the beach are treacherous so be prepared. Part required scrambling on all fours. It was worth it for us

reviews.title: The Best of Nusa Penida
reviews.text: Kelingking Beach would definitely mesmerize anyone upon seeing the natural formations. If you really want to get to the beach, you need to climb down thousand of steps that are very steep. You'll also need to allot 2-4 hours so that you could enjoy the beach because once you get finished, you'll climb the thousands of steps whence you came. If you'll stay at the top and take pictures, make sure you bring water as it is very hot throughout the day.

reviews.title: It's even more beautiful than the Photos
reviews.text: We went here twice and would recommend the same to you. We went for the sunset, parked and walked to the view point, we didn't have to pay for some reason, I think the people went home. However, we caught the sunset at perfect timing, I believe it was around 5 PM. A lot of people at the viewpoint and a lot of people walking up, they seemed so tired. Which made us a bit nervous about our next day. However, we didn't have any issues with the trek down. Take it slow! Don't get discouraged with all the people at the view point hardly anyone was actually walking down! Best time to the hike is later afternoon when it's not so hot and then you can walk up at sunset! Best way! Maybe 20 people on the beach. We would recommend not doing it in sandals we had Keen water shoes that we great for the trek! This is a must!

reviews.title: One of my best adventure
reviews.text: Breathtaking place. I was one of the few people who went down to the beach. It was not easy at all, so be careful if you are not fit enough with good health. I found one guy on his way back laying down and can't breathe well or move, so many good. People help him restore his energy.Not to scare you, just do it if are fit and prepared well.Fore me something to remember it all my life.

reviews.title: Sunset View
reviews.text: Amazing Sunset view! Estimate travel time around 1 hour from the port to reach here. Even is not far but the road condition will slow you down.I'm so happy that we have come here. it feel like so blessed to have this nice view together with your loved one.We bring some beer and light food sitting down and wait until sunset start. When sunset start it will be very fast, we are so happy that we able see it!True is, this place is dangerous. Once wrong step then you will say goodbye to the world. Please be careful if you have kids. It is extremely dangerous if didn't watch closely.You can go down to the beach but it is dangerous. The strong wave actually bring down few life before. The light is limited at this island. If you are not familiar, please rent you driver.

reviews.title: Impressive view
reviews.text: Pro - nice scenery, windy, beautiful beach. Cons: only if the steps are fixed properly. Advise: You can spend longer time here and trek down to the beach, I believe it has awesome wave.

reviews.title: Must see
reviews.text: Getting up and down to the beach not impossible, but tiring for sure (esp under bright burning sun). If you simply wanna take photos of T Rex from all angles, you dont need to walk all the way down. Instead you can go along the cafes and there is a farmland nearby where there are plenty of quiet but nice viewpoints of T Rex too.

reviews.title: Nice Cliff formation
reviews.text: Beautiful Cliff formation thst surroinds a beach. Make sure you get there as early as possible to beat the heat and the hundreds of turists. Prepared for the bumpy roads

reviews.title: Breathtaking view
reviews.text: Love it so much. Nice sea and cliffs . It Super hot but worth going. Expect to climb up n down to get a great view

reviews.title: Breathtaking
reviews.text: It’s not easy getting down and back up to/from the beach but it is well worth it. Not overcrowded and just stunning.

reviews.title: Walk down to the beach if you can
reviews.text: This was by far the highlight of our vacation. While it is a crazy hike down and up and the heat is sweltering, the picturesque views at the bottom are well worth it. The sand is perfect, one can cool off in the water and the beach in general is isolated. If you’re on a tour of Kelingking, billabong beach, and crystal bay, be sure to spend the majority of your time here as the other locations pale in comparison.

reviews.title: Amazing and so worth it
reviews.text: Be warned, exercise is a must :)The journey down the stairs to kelingking beach is quite difficult, so if you get exhausted easily, don’t try, as you need to go back up and it’s very steep. No other way except for the steep stairs. Half way down the mountain the stairs stop and it becomes more of a mountain climb but it has a handrail the whole time to assist in going down and back up. The beach down the bottom was totally worth the journey though as the water was perfectly clear and great for swimming in. There is a shop at the bottom that sells drinks and snacks also, as you will need refreshments after the exhausting climb down.

reviews.title: Paradise for sure
reviews.text: So your trip begin with the place where millions of people try to take the best photo of them, you may think that there is no place for you, but it’s not true, people do it very fast and you at least take a photo , a view is incredible for sure. Then you have an opportunity to go down to the beach , but be ready the way to beach is not for children ( I was surprised when I saw 8years old boy with father, it’s crazy) and people with health issues, because it’s a way under the sun for 30-35 min . When you go down or up you meet the people behind and front of you, the way is too narrow , so please be careful and put hiking shoes on. Don’t forget about water!!!!Finally when you already reach your destination point , it’s worth it, because you are in paradise with amazing view and enormous waves .So, you can do it, but be careful and stay positive

reviews.title: Very crowded
reviews.text: The view point is quite picturesque and is simply one of the best views one gets in Indonesia, but is so much crowded that you wont feel like staying for a bit and is close to get spoiled sooner. One would struggle to get a picture with clear background.Expect a lot of driving, through bad roads, to reach to the point and is quite a walk to reach the view point.

reviews.title: Gorgeous but be prepared to hike!
reviews.text: Incredible natural formation with crystal blue water and a flawless beach. Those expecting to swim in the water beware! Tides and currenst are extremely strong and not recommended for swimming. The hike down toward the beach is strenuous, with no shade available. Bring water and appropriate shoes and a small umbrella if you can!

reviews.title: Great Scenery
reviews.text: Becoming a definite tour destination with a crazy amount of motorbikes, vans and cars pouring into the area on narrow challenging roads.Once there, through the crowds it is a stunning view.

reviews.title: Beautiful view, so MANY people!!!
reviews.text: If you're thinking of motorbiking here from anywhere, rethink that and get a driver. The road is seriously bad and 15 miles turns into a hour drive to avoid the pot holes. Get here super early. As crowds get here around 9 am and parking is hard to find as well as getting a decent picture of T-Rex rock or the beach . The view is stunning, the water is the most beautiful blue. There area has few view vistas to get your picture, however lines can be long and you can easily wait 15 mins for your 15 seconds. I stayed for about 15 mins before the crowds were overwhelming.There is a few warungs located here so food and drinks are plentiful. The hike down to the beach is around 30 minutes from the top but we opted not to do it.

reviews.title: Breathtaking for sure!
reviews.text: What an experience to be able to get to this place and finally be able to lean over the cliff. The pictures are amazing but do not do any justice to the actual view. Good luck going down :)

reviews.title: World class natural landmark
reviews.text: Breathtaking. A must see for the world traveller. To walk down is for able bodied experienced walkers and swimmers. Not for the faint hearted as is it a sheer cliff of several hundred metres. 30 mins down, over an hour back up. Those not able or wanting to go down can still get the best photos of their lives from the top. Cold refreshments available near the car park.

reviews.title: Beautiful view
reviews.text: We came at 8 AM and there were o ly few other people. Lovely view. We didn't go down, because I've heard you have to slide some of the way down. They had new roads so it wasn't a problem driving scooter all the way there

reviews.title: Stunning Views
reviews.text: We arrived at Kelingking Beach early, before all the day-trippers, which I highly recommend. The view is absolutely stunning! We hiked only about 1/3 of the way down. The stairs are very steep and uneven. If you want to go the entire route they say it takes about 40 minutes to get down and an hour to get back up.Make sure to check out the view to the left of all of the restaurants. You can also get stunning pictures from that area.

reviews.title: one of the most beautiful beaches
reviews.text: This trail will not be any easier, this trail will be rocky and difficult - this is absolutely perfect for kelingking beach!  If you want to get down in the heat and get back up - it has to be really good and fit, but it's worth it!  However, climbing is announced here and is not without danger!  So not suitable for everyone.  away down we needed 30 min and high 20 min.  exhausting but who made it, can be proud of itself.  The view from the top is of course unique and must be visited, if you are on Nusa Penida.

reviews.title: Breathtaking
reviews.text: Firstly, the road to get to this place is very reasonable compared to many in Penida.  That’s a bonus.  So you could scooter from the harbour to hear no worries. Now this place was just to beautiful.  There are many viewing spots for this place.  You can pay a 5000rp donation to go up to a viewing platform which I did and stayed there as it was magnificent.  I launched the drone from up there too.  I did lose some gps a bit when I went high so had to bring it down a bit.  Plus I am not a very experienced drone pilot. There are monkeys here too so if you’re scared get someone to shoe them away for you.  There’s plenty of warungs to eat or drink at.  Parking tip - they charge and then point you to a parking area, however you can ride closer down and park elsewhere.  This is an absolute must see in Penida.  We did not go down to the beach, however I believe it takes about 30-45 mins down and same up.  On sometimes vertical track where you have to slide on your bum.  Not for me.  You need to be super fit to go down to the beach.

reviews.title: Go - but be prepared!
reviews.text: We went in low season, but even then it was busy with Instagram warriors queuing up in sweltering heat for once spot at the top of the cliff. Ignore these clowns and walk about 100m down the cliff for the same if that's what you're there for.The preparation part: if you want to actually go on to the beach it's roughly a 25 min, relatively intense walk/climb down. Do not attempt in flip-flops, and bring a bottle of water each. There are choke points where you'll have to wait 5+ mins for people to go up/down, and it is very steep at points. Essentially they've tacted barriers onto quite a sheer cliff face.It's well worth the climb however. The beach was relatively quiet (note again low season), has a shop for drinks and light snacks.The waves were powerful. It's not a beach for chilled floating around unless you swim past the sand bar and break. (Which is totally do able). Also be aware there is a strong rip tide.Had a great time, it's very clear water aside the sand being churned up and refreshingly cool.

reviews.title: Stunning view, well worth a visit
reviews.text: I have to admit, having been in Nusa Penida for a few days I couldn’t be bothered to do the 45 min trek down to the actual beach itself (what people who had just done the trip told me) having done so many of the hikes for the other stuff on the island I was just happy to look over the stunning view. The beach looks insane, so kind of gutted I didn’t go down! No one was in the water and the waves seem too powerful to swim.... which is what the below reviews also say. Absolutely stunning view and a must visit.

reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.text: The view at Kelingking Beach is stunning!The place is quite busy with tourists but not overly packed. You can choose to descend the steep flight of stairs to the beach itself. But make sure you leave enough energy to climb back up! 😄Not much activities here to do there except to admire the beautiful scenery.

reviews.title: Stunning!!
reviews.text: What an amazing spot!  Water colour is stunning. White sand. Clean beach. Waves can be rough so you need to be careful. The climb up and down is for the fit otherwise it will be a struggle coming up. It is very steep and can be narrow in parts. Most of the track is made from clay so it isn’t man made ‘stairs’. We wore thongs going down, not a good idea! And we put our joggers on coming back up. If you have joggers definitely wear them. Take water a large one with you in a backpack as you will need both hands free for the climb. There is water on sale on the beach but I believe it is expensive. Only toilets are at the top of the cliff none on the beach. Do this as early as you can as it is very hot climbing. Definitely worth seeing.

reviews.title: Mind-blowing view !!
reviews.text: Hands down one of the most beautiful places one can see. The colors of the water from up above the cliff is mesmerizing to say the least.A must visit place when in Bali/Nusa Penida. Just come prepared with good shoes and water as it can be too hot.

reviews.title: Nusa Penida Tour
reviews.text: Our trip in Nusa Penida was unforgettable moment, thanks to Mustika Nusa Penida Tour especially to Sir Dewarai, very accomodating and he knows the good spot for picture for instagram ! Super thank you kuya ! You're the best ! I will recommend this Mustika Nusa Penida Tour can speak english and very accomodating

reviews.title: Finally Can See the Beautiful Beach
reviews.text: The Second time, this still recommended Beach. Clean Beach, Nice Beach, Nice Sunset in Here. Must try to go down.

reviews.title: Kelingking Beach is Amazing!
reviews.text: Kelingking Beach is absolutely stunning, but the hike down the mountain path is not for the faint hearted or the unfit.The path down starts of reasonably easy, after 20 mins or so it takes a turn back on its self and then the fun really starts.
